a1.name: Ancient Civilizations
a1.summary: Writing and cities arose, and the first dynasties and empires appeared across the world.
a1.catch: Writing and cities lit up the world
features: Civilizations of Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus and the Yellow River
Writing, calendars and law emerge
City-states centered on kings and temples
Bronze reshapes the balance of power

a2.name: Classical Antiquity
a2.summary: Greece, Rome, Han China and Persia stood side by side as great empires, and ideas and religions took root.
a2.catch: An age of ideas and empires
features: Greek democracy and philosophy
Rome unites the Mediterranean
The great empires of Qin–Han, Persia and India
Buddhism, Confucianism and Christianity take root

a3.name: Middle Ages
a3.summary: The Islamic world and the Mongols linked East and West, while Europe stirred out of feudal society.
a3.catch: Faith and trade connect the world
features: Islamic empires link East and West
The Mongols cross Eurasia
Feudal Europe and the Crusades
The Black Death spreads across the world

a4.name: Age of Exploration & Early Modern
a4.summary: The sea joined the world together as silver, crops, diseases and enslaved people crossed the oceans.
a4.catch: The sea made the world one
features: Portugal and Spain open new sea routes
Conquest of the Americas and the flow of silver
Crops, diseases and slaves travel between continents
The Reformation and printing spread ideas

a5.name: Revolutions & Empires
a5.summary: Industrial and civic revolutions changed the world while the Great Powers expanded their colonies.
features: Civic revolutions and nation-states
The Industrial Revolution and the rise of capitalism
The Powers carve up Africa and Asia
Abolition of slavery and the ideal of human rights

a6.name: The Two World Wars
a6.summary: Total war, depression and revolution remade the world order.
a6.catch: Total war and a shaken world
features: World War I and the Russian Revolution
The Great Depression and the rise of fascism
World War II and the Holocaust
Atomic bombs change warfare

a7.name: Contemporary Era
a7.summary: After the Cold War, decolonization and globalization, an age of interdependence.
a7.catch: From the Cold War to interdependence
features: The US–Soviet Cold War and nuclear balance
Independence of Asian and African nations
Globalization and the internet
Crises chain across borders

as_sumer.title: Mesopotamian Civilization
as_sumer.detail: Cities and writing (cuneiform) arose between the Tigris and Euphrates.
as_sumer.lesson: The technology of record-keeping made states and law possible.

af_egypt.title: Unification of Egypt
af_egypt.detail: A unified dynasty formed along the Nile and the pharaohs' rule began.
af_egypt.lesson: The yearly flood fostered calendars, surveying and bureaucracy.

af_pyramid.title: Great Pyramid
af_pyramid.detail: King Khufu's colossal tomb was built, displaying royal power.
af_pyramid.lesson: Monumental building also proves a state's power to mobilize people.

as_indus.title: Indus Civilization
as_indus.detail: A civilization that built planned cities such as Mohenjo-daro.
as_indus.lesson: Despite advanced urban design, its script remains undeciphered.

as_yin.title: Shang Dynasty
as_yin.detail: One of China's earliest dynasties, with bronzes and oracle-bone script.
as_yin.lesson: A theocratic state that decided policy by divination.

am_olmec.title: Olmec Civilization
am_olmec.detail: One of Mesoamerica's earliest civilizations, known for colossal stone heads.
am_olmec.lesson: Regarded as a wellspring of later Maya and Aztec culture.

as_chunqiu.title: Spring and Autumn Period
as_chunqiu.detail: The Zhou declined and lords entered a long era of rivalry for hegemony.
as_chunqiu.lesson: The turmoil produced a bumper crop of ideas: the Hundred Schools of Thought.

af_kush.title: Kingdom of Kush
af_kush.detail: Nubian kings ruled Egypt and founded the 25th Dynasty.

as_confucius.title: Confucius
as_confucius.detail: A thinker who taught government by virtue and ritual was born.
as_confucius.lesson: Confucianism shaped East Asian rule and family values for two thousand years.

as_achaemenid.title: Achaemenid Empire
as_achaemenid.detail: Persia unified western Asia, ruling a vast area through roads and provinces.
as_achaemenid.lesson: A model of governance that loosely bound diverse peoples together.

eu_athens.title: Athenian Democracy
eu_athens.detail: Cleisthenes' reforms let citizens take part directly in politics.
eu_athens.lesson: The origin of sharing power among citizens—though women and slaves were excluded.

as_buddha.title: Rise of Buddhism
as_buddha.detail: Gautama Siddhartha attained enlightenment and taught release from suffering.
as_buddha.lesson: It became a world religion spreading from India across Asia.

eu_persianwar.title: Persian Wars
eu_persianwar.detail: Greek cities resisted the great eastern empire and won at Marathon and Salamis.
eu_persianwar.lesson: Beating a great power as a small alliance nourished the city-states' pride.

eu_alex.title: Alexander's Eastern Campaign
eu_alex.detail: The Macedonian king marched east, ruling from Egypt to northwest India.
eu_alex.lesson: Conquest produced a blending of cultures (Hellenism).

af_alexandria.title: Alexandria
af_alexandria.detail: Alexander founded a port city that grew into a center of learning.
af_alexandria.lesson: Its library and research institute gathered Greek and Eastern knowledge.

eu_punic.title: Punic Wars
eu_punic.detail: Rome and Carthage fought for supremacy in the Mediterranean, and Rome won.
eu_punic.lesson: Whoever commands the sea commands the trade sphere.

as_qin.title: Qin Unification
as_qin.detail: The First Emperor unified China for the first time and standardized script and measures.
as_qin.lesson: The forced unification was short-lived, but the commandery system endured.

af_carthage.title: Fall of Carthage
af_carthage.detail: Rome took the city and the Phoenician-descended maritime state vanished.
af_carthage.lesson: History came down to us written from the victors' side.

as_silkroad.title: Zhang Qian's Journey West
as_silkroad.detail: A Han envoy traveled to the Western Regions, opening the way to the later Silk Road.
as_silkroad.lesson: An envoy's journey ended up creating the artery of East–West trade.

af_ptolemy.title: Egypt Becomes a Roman Province
af_ptolemy.detail: After Cleopatra's death, Egypt became a Roman province.
af_ptolemy.lesson: As Rome's granary, it sustained the empire.

eu_empire.title: Roman Empire
eu_empire.detail: Augustus became the first emperor and the empire ringing the Mediterranean stabilized.
eu_empire.lesson: Shifting to autocracy while keeping republican forms became both model and cautionary tale.

as_gandhara.title: Gandhara Art
as_gandhara.detail: Buddha images began to be made using Greek-style techniques.
as_gandhara.lesson: Cultures mix where they meet, giving birth to new forms.

as_jp_wa.title: Receiving the Gold Seal
as_jp_wa.detail: A Wa envoy from Nu is recorded as receiving a seal from the Han emperor.
as_jp_wa.lesson: Japan's records first appear in foreign chronicles.

eu_antoninus.title: Envoys from Daqin
eu_antoninus.detail: A party claiming to be Roman imperial envoys is recorded reaching Han China.
eu_antoninus.lesson: The two ends of the Silk Road first learned of each other by name.

as_jp_himiko.title: Himiko Sends Envoys to Wei
as_jp_himiko.detail: The queen of Wa sent an embassy to Wei and received the title "King of Wa, Friend of Wei."
as_jp_himiko.lesson: Diplomacy was used to build authority at home.

am_maya.title: Maya Classic Period
am_maya.detail: The Maya peak began, with stone cities, calendars and writing.
am_maya.lesson: They had advanced astronomy yet used neither ironwork nor the wheel.

eu_christ.title: Toleration of Christianity
eu_christ.detail: The Edict of Milan ended persecution and led later to state religion.
eu_christ.lesson: A persecuted minority became the empire's religion.

af_axum.title: Conversion of Axum
af_axum.detail: The kingdom on the Ethiopian highlands accepted Christianity.
af_axum.lesson: One of Africa's oldest Christian states left a church that lives on today.

eu_split.title: Division of the Roman Empire
eu_split.detail: The empire was governed as East and West and was never reunited.
eu_split.lesson: A giant organization can sometimes survive only by being split.

eu_fall.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
eu_fall.detail: A Germanic mercenary commander deposed the last emperor.
eu_fall.lesson: The marker dividing the end of antiquity from the start of the Middle Ages.

as_jp_buddhism.title: Introduction of Buddhism to Japan
as_jp_buddhism.detail: Buddha images and scriptures are said to have come from Baekje.
as_jp_buddhism.lesson: A continental religion also became a bone of political contention.

as_tang.title: Founding of the Tang
as_tang.detail: East Asia's central empire, flourishing in law codes and urban culture.
as_tang.lesson: Neighbors built their states by studying Tang institutions.

as_hijra.title: Rise of Islam
as_hijra.detail: Muhammad moved to Medina and the Islamic community was founded.
as_hijra.lesson: Faith and politics joined and spread rapidly.

as_jp_kento.title: Japanese Embassies to Tang
as_jp_kento.detail: Japan sent envoys and students to Tang to learn its institutions and culture.
as_jp_kento.lesson: They kept learning, choosing what to study and changing how.

af_islam_north.title: Islamization of North Africa
af_islam_north.detail: Arab armies advanced into North Africa and over centuries language and religion changed.
af_islam_north.lesson: Trade routes to sub-Saharan Africa carried Islam too.

as_umayyad.title: Umayyad Caliphate
as_umayyad.detail: The Islamic empire stretched west to North Africa and Iberia.
as_umayyad.lesson: Arabic and faith became a common base linking a vast area.

eu_tours.title: Battle of Tours
eu_tours.detail: The Frankish kingdom halted the northward push of Islamic forces.
eu_tours.lesson: The boundary between Western Europe and the Islamic world was fixed.

as_talas.title: Battle of Talas
as_talas.detail: Tang and the Abbasids clashed, and papermaking is said to have reached the Islamic world.
as_talas.lesson: Technology moves through battles and prisoners too.

eu_franks.title: Coronation of Charlemagne
eu_franks.detail: The pope crowned the Frankish king emperor of the Romans.
eu_franks.lesson: The fusion of Rome, the Germanic peoples and Christianity became the core of Western Europe.

af_ghana.title: Kingdom of Ghana
af_ghana.detail: It prospered in West Africa trading gold and salt across the Sahara.
af_ghana.lesson: Trade across the desert gave rise to a great power.

as_wisdom.title: House of Wisdom
as_wisdom.detail: In Baghdad, Greek and other scholarly works were translated into Arabic.
as_wisdom.lesson: Translation preserved knowledge, which later flowed back to Europe.

as_seljuk.title: Battle of Manzikert
as_seljuk.detail: The Seljuks defeated Byzantium and advanced into Asia Minor.
as_seljuk.lesson: Byzantium's call for help was one trigger of the Crusades.

eu_crusade.title: The Crusades
eu_crusade.detail: At the pope's call, expeditions to retake the Holy Land of Jerusalem began.
eu_crusade.lesson: Religious zeal entwined with vested interests, deepening East–West contact and conflict.

af_zimbabwe.title: Great Zimbabwe
af_zimbabwe.detail: A stone city was built in southern Africa and thrived on gold and ivory trade.
af_zimbabwe.lesson: In colonial times, its stone ruins were refused credit as African-built.

as_mongol.title: Mongol Empire
as_mongol.detail: Under Genghis Khan an empire spanning Eurasia was built.
as_mongol.lesson: Conquest brought destruction, but also opened safe roads for East–West exchange.

eu_magna.title: Magna Carta
eu_magna.detail: A document in which barons made the king accept limits on his power.
eu_magna.lesson: A source of constitutionalism: even the king is under the law.

as_jp_mongol.title: Mongol Invasions of Japan
as_jp_mongol.detail: Yuan and Goryeo forces attacked Kyushu (the Bun'ei and Koan invasions).
as_jp_mongol.lesson: The problem of rewarding defenders shook the Kamakura shogunate.

as_marcopolo.title: Marco Polo
as_marcopolo.detail: A Venetian merchant reached Khanbaliq and later left an account of his travels.
as_marcopolo.lesson: One travelogue shaped Europeans' image of and longing for Asia.

as_ottoman.title: Ottoman Empire
as_ottoman.detail: A state that arose in Anatolia grew into a great empire spanning three continents.
as_ottoman.lesson: Holding the gateway of East–West trade, it spurred Europe's search for sea routes.

af_mali.title: Gold of Mali
af_mali.detail: The king of Mali made a pilgrimage to Mecca with vast gold, and his wealth became known in the Mediterranean.
af_mali.lesson: The existence of gold turned European interest toward Africa.

am_aztec.title: Tenochtitlan
am_aztec.detail: A city on a lake was built and later became the center of the Aztec kingdom.
am_aztec.lesson: Its population is said to have rivaled Europe's largest cities of the time.

eu_plague.title: Black Death
eu_plague.detail: Plague swept through, and about a third of Europe's population is said to have been lost.
eu_plague.lesson: Labor shortages raised the status of serfs and shook the Church's authority.

as_ming.title: Founding of the Ming
as_ming.detail: Mongol rule ended and a Han Chinese dynasty returned.
as_ming.lesson: It managed foreign relations through sea bans and the tribute system.

eu_renaissance.title: Renaissance
eu_renaissance.detail: A movement to study classical antiquity anew spread from Italian cities.
eu_renaissance.lesson: It was also a rediscovery of knowledge preserved by other civilizations (the Islamic world).

af_swahili.title: Swahili Coast
af_swahili.detail: East African port towns prospered on Indian Ocean trade, mixing Arab, Persian and African cultures.
af_swahili.lesson: Exchange across the sea gave birth to a distinctive language and culture.

as_zhenghe.title: Zheng He's Voyages
as_zhenghe.detail: A great Ming fleet crossed the Indian Ocean, reaching as far as East Africa.
as_zhenghe.lesson: It displayed overwhelming national power without colonizing.

am_inca.title: Inca Empire
am_inca.detail: An empire with a road network and administration spread across the Andes.
am_inca.lesson: Lacking writing, it managed information with knotted cords (quipu).

eu_print.title: Movable-Type Printing
eu_print.detail: Gutenberg made printing with movable type practical.
eu_print.lesson: Cheaper copying of information spread knowledge and ideas all at once.

eu_byz_fall.title: Fall of Byzantium
eu_byz_fall.lesson: Trade routes in the eastern Mediterranean changed and eyes turned to the Atlantic.

af_cape.title: Reaching the Cape of Good Hope
af_cape.detail: Portugal's Dias reached the southern tip of Africa.
af_cape.lesson: The African coast became a waystation linking Europe with other regions.

eu_columbus.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
eu_columbus.detail: A voyage westward toward Asia reached islands in the Caribbean.
eu_columbus.lesson: A chance arrival permanently joined two worlds.

am_exchange.title: Columbian Exchange
am_exchange.detail: Crops, livestock and pathogens moved between the Old and New Worlds.
am_exchange.lesson: Potatoes and maize supported world population, while smallpox devastated native peoples.

as_gama.title: Da Gama Reaches India
as_gama.detail: Portugal reached India by the route around the southern tip of Africa.
as_gama.lesson: European powers entered the spice trade of the Indian Ocean directly.

af_timbuktu.title: Timbuktu
af_timbuktu.detail: A West African trading city flourished as a center of Islamic scholarship.
af_timbuktu.lesson: Its manuscripts survive today, telling the history of African knowledge.

af_slave.title: Atlantic Slave Trade
af_slave.detail: Vast numbers of people were forcibly taken from Africa to the Americas.
af_slave.lesson: A system that made people into goods tied together the economies of several continents.

eu_reform.title: Reformation
eu_reform.detail: Luther criticized the Church and Protestants split off.
eu_reform.lesson: The printing press amplified ideas across borders.

am_aztec_fall.title: Fall of the Aztecs
am_aztec_fall.detail: Spanish forces under Cortés took the capital with native allies and smallpox on their side.
am_aztec_fall.lesson: Disease and internal conflict mattered as much as weapons.

as_mughal.title: Mughal Empire
as_mughal.detail: An Islamic dynasty arose in northern India and integrated diverse cultures.
as_mughal.lesson: Rule across religious differences nurtured a distinctive culture.

am_inca_fall.title: Fall of the Inca
am_inca_fall.detail: Pizarro captured the emperor and the empire collapsed.
am_inca_fall.lesson: The chaos just after a civil war made conquest easy.

as_jp_gun.title: Arrival of Firearms in Japan
as_jp_gun.detail: Portuguese drifted to Tanegashima and muskets were introduced.
as_jp_gun.lesson: New technology was domesticated quickly and changed the shape of war.

am_silver.title: Potosí Silver Mine
am_silver.detail: A huge silver mine was found in the Andes, changing the flow of the world's silver.
am_silver.lesson: Silver crossed the Atlantic and Pacific and poured into China's economy.

as_eic.title: East India Companies
as_eic.detail: Britain and others founded trading companies as bases for entering Asia.
as_eic.lesson: A forerunner of colonial rule, with companies holding armies and governing power.

am_plantation.title: Plantations
am_plantation.detail: Big sugar and tobacco estates spread on the labor of people brought from Africa.
am_plantation.lesson: Industry reliant on cheap labor underpinned Britain's capital accumulation.

eu_westphalia.title: Peace of Westphalia
eu_westphalia.detail: The Thirty Years' War ended and an order of coexisting sovereign states emerged.
eu_westphalia.lesson: Regarded as the starting point of modern international relations.

eu_newton.title: Newtonian Mechanics
eu_newton.detail: The Principia was published and the move to explain nature mathematically became decisive.
eu_newton.lesson: The Scientific Revolution became the basis of the later Industrial Revolution.

eu_enlight.title: Enlightenment
eu_enlight.detail: Ideas valuing reason and liberty spread in France and elsewhere.
eu_enlight.lesson: A habit of questioning authority became the ideological fuel of revolution.

eu_indrev.title: Industrial Revolution
eu_indrev.detail: Steam engines and mechanization began an industrial society in Britain.
eu_indrev.lesson: The craving for productive power, resources and markets covered the world in colonies.

am_indep.title: American Independence
am_indep.detail: Thirteen colonies declared independence and built a republic.
am_indep.lesson: One of the earliest cases of turning Enlightenment thought into an actual constitution.

eu_french.title: French Revolution
eu_french.detail: A revolution toppled the estates system and proclaimed the rights of man.
eu_french.lesson: Its ideals crossed borders and influenced independence and revolutions elsewhere.

af_napoleon_egypt.title: Egyptian Expedition
af_napoleon_egypt.detail: Napoleon's army landed and serious contact between modern Europe and Egypt began.
af_napoleon_egypt.lesson: Scholars who accompanied the expedition found the Rosetta Stone.

eu_napoleon.title: Napoleonic Empire
eu_napoleon.detail: A soldier of the Revolution became emperor and spread law and war across Europe.
eu_napoleon.lesson: Turmoil at home created an opening for colonial independence.

am_haiti.title: Haitian Independence
am_haiti.detail: A revolution of enslaved people founded the world's first Black republic.
am_haiti.lesson: Independence went unrecognized, and a huge indemnity was imposed.

am_latin.title: Latin American Independence
am_latin.detail: Under leaders such as Bolívar, the Spanish colonies won independence one after another.
am_latin.lesson: Turmoil in the mother country was the chance for independence movements.

am_monroe.title: Monroe Doctrine
am_monroe.detail: The United States declared opposition to European interference in the Americas.
am_monroe.lesson: It later became grounds for US interventionism.

as_opium.title: Opium War
as_opium.detail: Britain and Qing fought; Qing lost, leading to open ports and the cession of Hong Kong.
as_opium.lesson: Fixing a trade deficit turned into the drug trade and war.

as_jp_perry.title: Arrival of Perry's Black Ships
as_jp_perry.detail: Perry's fleet arrived at Uraga and pressed Japan to open.
as_jp_perry.lesson: Outside pressure set the domestic political system in motion.

am_civil.title: American Civil War
am_civil.detail: North and South fought over slavery, and the North won.
am_civil.lesson: Abolishing the system did not end racial discrimination afterward.

as_jp_meiji.title: Meiji Restoration
as_jp_meiji.detail: The shogunate fell and modern nation-building advanced all at once.
as_jp_meiji.lesson: Rapid reform to keep independence while learning from the West.

af_suez.title: Suez Canal
af_suez.detail: A canal joining the Mediterranean and Red Sea opened, greatly shortening Europe–Asia routes.
af_suez.lesson: Control of the canal later invited British intervention.

eu_berlinconf.title: Berlin Conference
eu_berlinconf.detail: The Powers set the rules for partitioning Africa without local representatives.
eu_berlinconf.lesson: The lines were drawn ignoring peoples and terrain.

af_partition.title: Scramble for Africa
af_partition.detail: The Powers divided nearly the whole continent among themselves as colonies.
af_partition.lesson: The borders remained a source of conflict even after independence.

af_adwa.title: Battle of Adwa
af_adwa.detail: Ethiopia defeated the Italian army and kept its independence.
af_adwa.lesson: One of the few cases of preserved African independence, it became a symbol for later movements.

as_xinhai.title: Xinhai Revolution
as_xinhai.detail: The Qing fell and Asia's first republic was founded.
as_xinhai.lesson: The end of empire was also the start of long civil strife.

eu_ww1.title: World War I
eu_ww1.detail: A chain of alliances and rivalries produced total war and tens of millions of casualties.
eu_ww1.lesson: Distortions in the postwar settlement seeded the next war.

eu_russia.title: Russian Revolution
eu_russia.detail: The monarchy fell and the world's first socialist state was founded.
eu_russia.lesson: The starting point of the axis of conflict known as the Cold War.

am_depression.title: Great Depression
am_depression.detail: A global slump began with the crash of the New York stock market.
am_depression.lesson: Protectionism spread among nations and fed political extremism.

as_manchuria.title: Manchurian Incident
as_manchuria.detail: The Kwantung Army occupied Manchuria, and Japan moved toward leaving the League of Nations.
as_manchuria.lesson: The government could not stop the army's runaway action in a crisis.

eu_nazi.title: Nazi Government
eu_nazi.detail: Dictatorship was established through legal procedures amid the Depression's turmoil.
eu_nazi.lesson: Economic anxiety joined with xenophobia can destroy a democracy from within.

am_newdeal.title: New Deal
am_newdeal.detail: Policies began in which the government sought recovery through public works and regulation.
am_newdeal.lesson: A shift from leaving it to the market to supporting it through the state.

eu_ww2.title: World War II
eu_ww2.detail: It began with Germany's invasion of Poland and became a global war.
eu_ww2.lesson: It shaped the postwar frameworks of the UN, human rights and the Cold War.

as_pacific.title: Pacific War
as_pacific.detail: Japan went to war with the US and Britain, and the battlefield spread across Asia and the Pacific.
as_pacific.lesson: The cost of a decision that discounted the gap in national strength with a great power was heavy.

am_manhattan.title: Manhattan Project
am_manhattan.detail: The US secretly developed the atomic bomb.
am_manhattan.lesson: Émigré scientists and a nation's total effort produced a new weapon.

as_atomic.title: Atomic Bombings
as_atomic.detail: Atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and Japan surrendered.
as_atomic.lesson: Nuclear weapons changed the nature of war and international politics.

eu_cold.title: Cold War
eu_cold.detail: East and West divided around the US and USSR, with nuclear balance and proxy wars.
eu_cold.lesson: A confrontation without direct fighting spread war to peripheral regions.

as_india_ind.title: Indian Independence
as_india_ind.detail: British India became independent, splitting into India and Pakistan.
as_india_ind.lesson: Partition came with mass migration and violence.

am_marshall.title: Marshall Plan
am_marshall.detail: The US gave huge aid to Western Europe's postwar recovery.
am_marshall.lesson: Economic aid was also a means of building blocs in the Cold War.

af_apartheid.title: Apartheid
af_apartheid.detail: Racial segregation was made law in South Africa.
af_apartheid.lesson: Institutional discrimination drew international condemnation and sanctions.

as_prc.title: People's Republic of China
as_prc.detail: After civil war, the Communist Party took power and the PRC was founded.
as_prc.lesson: It transformed the map of power in Cold War Asia.

as_korea.title: Korean War
as_korea.detail: The US and China joined the fight between North and South Korea, fixing the division.
as_korea.lesson: The first case in Asia of the Cold War turning hot.

as_bandung.title: Bandung Conference
as_bandung.detail: Twenty-nine Asian and African nations met and opposed colonialism.
as_bandung.lesson: A third voice beyond the US and USSR first appeared in world politics.

af_suezcrisis.title: Suez Crisis
af_suezcrisis.detail: Egypt nationalized the canal, and Britain, France and Israel intervened.
af_suezcrisis.lesson: The limits of the old colonial powers showed the era led by the US and USSR.

eu_eec.title: Treaty of Rome
eu_eec.detail: The European Economic Community began and later grew into the EU.
eu_eec.lesson: An attempt to bind nations through economics so as not to repeat war.

af_year.title: Year of Africa
af_year.detail: Seventeen countries became independent at once and the colonial system largely crumbled.
af_year.lesson: Even after independence, problems of economic structure and borders remained.

af_algeria.title: Algerian Independence
af_algeria.detail: After an eight-year war of independence, Algeria became independent from France.
af_algeria.lesson: The war of decolonization left deep wounds in the former metropole's society too.

am_cuba.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
am_cuba.detail: Over Soviet missile deployment, the US and USSR stood on the brink of nuclear war.
am_cuba.lesson: In the end, dialogue and compromise avoided catastrophe.

am_civilrights.title: Civil Rights Act
am_civilrights.detail: A law prohibiting racial discrimination was enacted.
am_civilrights.lesson: Accumulated movements changed the law, but discrimination persists.

as_vietnam.title: Vietnam War
as_vietnam.detail: US forces intervened in earnest in one of the Cold War's largest proxy wars.
as_vietnam.lesson: Overwhelming military power does not always yield political victory.

am_moon.title: Moon Landing
am_moon.detail: Apollo 11 sent humans to the Moon.
am_moon.lesson: Technological competition in the Cold War accelerated space development.

as_oil.title: Oil Crisis
as_oil.detail: After a Middle East war, crude oil prices soared and shook the world economy.
as_oil.lesson: The uneven distribution of resources shook the growth myth of advanced nations.

as_reform.title: Reform and Opening
as_reform.detail: China adopted a market economy and entered an era of high growth.
as_reform.lesson: It became the world's factory and changed the shape of the international division of labor.

eu_berlin.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
eu_berlin.detail: The symbol of East–West division was opened by ordinary citizens.
eu_berlin.lesson: The end of a regime can come as if suddenly.

eu_ussr.title: Collapse of the Soviet Union
eu_ussr.detail: The union was dissolved and the Cold War ended.
eu_ussr.lesson: Unipolarity and the revival of ethnic problems occurred at once.

af_mandela.title: Mandela Presidency
af_mandela.detail: Apartheid was abolished and a government was born from an election open to all races.
af_mandela.lesson: A transition that chose reconciliation over revenge gave the world hope.

af_rwanda.title: Rwandan Genocide
af_rwanda.detail: In about a hundred days, hundreds of thousands or more were killed.
af_rwanda.lesson: Ethnic categories fixed in the colonial era formed the background of the tragedy.

am_internet.title: Spread of the Internet
am_internet.detail: The Web spread to the public and began to change information and commerce.
am_internet.lesson: Military and academic technology, opened to the public, changed the world.

eu_euro.title: Introduction of the Euro
eu_euro.detail: Many European countries adopted a single currency.
eu_euro.lesson: It carried a weakness: unified money but separate fiscal policies.

af_china.title: China–Africa Cooperation
af_china.detail: China expanded economic ties with Africa, and trade and investment surged.
af_china.lesson: The new relationship has stirred debate over aid and debt.

as_afghan.title: Afghanistan Invasion
as_afghan.detail: In retaliation for the 9/11 attacks, US forces attacked Afghanistan.
as_afghan.lesson: After twenty years of war, the regime returned to what it was.

am_911.title: September 11 Attacks
am_911.detail: Four airliners were hijacked in the US and about 3,000 people died.
am_911.lesson: The war on terror left long-term effects across several regions.

af_au.title: African Union
af_au.detail: The OAU was reorganized to pursue integration and joint problem-solving among African states.
af_au.lesson: Integration is an attempt to overcome divisions inherited from colonialism.

am_2008.title: Lehman Crisis
am_2008.detail: The collapse of US housing finance grew into a global financial crisis.
am_2008.lesson: Complex financial products spread the crisis worldwide.

eu_debt.title: European Debt Crisis
eu_debt.detail: Greece's fiscal problems spread into credit anxiety across the whole eurozone.

eu_ukraine.title: Invasion of Ukraine
eu_ukraine.detail: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine and European security was shaken.
eu_ukraine.lesson: Effects reached distant regions through energy and food.

w3_001.title: Code of Hammurabi
w3_001.detail: Babylonian king Hammurabi had 282 laws carved on a stele and made public. It is known for "an eye for an eye."
w3_001.lesson: Writing laws down and publishing them was a first step in binding arbitrary power.

w3_002.title: Battle of Kadesh
w3_002.detail: Egypt's Ramesses II and the Hittites fought a huge chariot battle in Syria. The peace treaty that followed is regarded as one of the oldest surviving international treaties.
w3_002.lesson: A battle with no winner gave birth to the invention of the treaty.

w3_003.title: Bronze Age Collapse
w3_003.detail: Invasions by the "Sea Peoples," famine and earthquakes combined, and states of the eastern Mediterranean such as the Hittites and Mycenaeans declined one after another.
w3_003.lesson: A tightly woven web collapses in a chain when one point is cut.

w3_004.title: Zhou Overthrow the Shang
w3_004.detail: King Wu of Zhou is said to have defeated the Shang at Muye and founded a new dynasty. The idea of the "Mandate of Heaven" was voiced.
w3_004.lesson: Tying the legitimacy of power to "Heaven" runs through all later Chinese history.

w3_005.title: First Olympic Games
w3_005.detail: Greek poleis gathered at Zeus's sanctuary of Olympia to compete. A custom held that fighting stopped during the games.
w3_005.lesson: Competition created a common culture among scattered cities.

w3_006.title: Legendary Founding of Rome
w3_006.detail: The traditional year when Romulus built a city on the banks of the Tiber. In reality a small settlement grew over a long time.
w3_006.lesson: The traditional date shows less the facts than how people wanted to tell their own story.

w3_007.title: Fall of Nineveh
w3_007.detail: A Neo-Babylonian and Median alliance took the Assyrian capital Nineveh. The great empire that ruled the Orient vanished quickly.
w3_007.lesson: Rule by terror keeps multiplying enemies around it.

w3_008.title: Babylonian Captivity
w3_008.detail: Nebuchadnezzar II of Neo-Babylonia took Jerusalem and deported the people of Judah. During captivity the compilation of Jewish scriptures is said to have advanced.
w3_008.lesson: A community that lost its homeland held itself together with books and faith.

w3_009.title: Founding of the Roman Republic
w3_009.detail: In tradition, the kings were expelled and a republic with elected consuls began. Mechanisms that did not concentrate power in one person were developed.
w3_009.lesson: The idea of dividing power and limiting terms became a prototype for later constitutions.

w3_010.title: Battle of Salamis
w3_010.detail: The Athenian general Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into a narrow strait and won a great victory. The rowers of the triremes were citizens.
w3_010.lesson: Citizens who fought at sea gained the voice that sustained democracy.

w3_011.title: Peloponnesian War
w3_011.detail: The Athens-led Delian League and the Sparta-led Peloponnesian League fought for about 27 years. The Greek world was exhausted and declined.
w3_011.lesson: A fight for hegemony wears out the victor too.

w3_012.title: Accession of Ashoka
w3_012.detail: Ashoka of the Maurya dynasty, regretting the carnage of the Kalinga War, turned to Buddhism and had rule by Dharma carved on pillars.
w3_012.lesson: Remorse over violence can give birth to a political ideal.

w3_013.title: Burning of Books and Burying of Scholars
w3_013.detail: To control thought, Qin Shi Huang is said to have burned all but practical books and buried scholars alive.
w3_013.lesson: Unifying thought firms up a state but thins out knowledge.

w3_014.title: Founding of the Han
w3_014.detail: Liu Bang defeated Xiang Yu at Gaixia and took the throne, founding the Han. He is known as an emperor of peasant origin.
w3_014.lesson: More than rank, the ability to employ people decided the realm.

w3_015.title: Battle of Zama
w3_015.detail: Scipio defeated Hannibal and ended the Second Punic War. Carthage lost its overseas territory and fleet.
w3_015.lesson: The one who studied the enemy's tactics and turned them around won in the end.

w3_016.title: Gracchi Reforms
w3_016.detail: The tribune Tiberius Gracchus tried to give land to impoverished citizens and was killed. Conflict within Rome began to tilt toward violence.
w3_016.lesson: The gap between rich and poor destroys a republic from the inside.

w3_017.title: Spartacus Revolt
w3_017.detail: The gladiator-slave Spartacus rose up and tens of thousands of slaves joined, repeatedly beating Roman armies before being put down at last.
w3_017.lesson: The anger of the ruled shook the ground under the empire.

w3_018.title: Assassination of Caesar
w3_018.detail: Senators claiming to defend the republic assassinated the dictator for life, Caesar, in the Senate. Civil war instead invited empire.
w3_018.lesson: An assassination out of fear of dictatorship produced a stronger one.

w3_019.title: Battle of Actium
w3_019.detail: Octavian's fleet defeated the combined forces of Antony and Cleopatra. Egypt was annexed the next year and Rome's civil wars ended.
w3_019.lesson: The end of civil war was the start of one victor's rule.

w3_020.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
w3_020.detail: Jesus is said to have been crucified under the Roman governor Pilate. Christianity spread from his disciples' accounts.
w3_020.lesson: An event in a small province changed the world's calendar and faith.

w3_021.title: Great Fire of Rome and Persecution of Christians
w3_021.detail: Emperor Nero is said to have blamed Christians for the fire that burned most of Rome.
w3_021.lesson: In anxious times, minorities are often made scapegoats.

w3_022.title: Destruction of the Jerusalem Temple
w3_022.detail: In the Jewish War, Roman troops burned the Second Temple. The life of the Jewish people, who would then disperse (the Diaspora), took shape.
w3_022.lesson: A people who lost their holy place survived by carrying their teachings and community with them.

w3_023.title: Eruption of Vesuvius
w3_023.detail: Ash and pyroclastic flows buried Pompeii and Herculaneum. The towns are being excavated just as daily life stood.
w3_023.lesson: A sudden disaster froze everyday life whole.

w3_024.title: Cai Lun Improves Paper
w3_024.detail: The Later Han eunuch Cai Lun is said to have made practical paper from bark and rags and presented it to the emperor.
w3_024.lesson: A cheap, light recording medium changed the speed at which knowledge spread.

w3_025.title: Roman Empire at Its Greatest Extent
w3_025.detail: Under Trajan, one of the Five Good Emperors, Roman territory reached its largest. Citizenship spread to provincials too.
w3_025.lesson: An overextended state also faces rising costs of defense.

w3_026.title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
w3_026.detail: Under the Way of Great Peace leader Zhang Jue, hundreds of thousands of peasants rose wearing yellow cloths. The Han was thus set toward regional generals gaining power and warlord rivalry.
w3_026.lesson: When faith joins with poverty, a great movement arises.

w3_027.title: Battle of Red Cliffs
w3_027.detail: On the Yangtze, the allied forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei defeated Cao Cao's great army. The course toward China's division into Wei, Wu and Shu was set.
w3_027.lesson: The outnumbered side won with terrain and fire attack.

w3_028.title: Founding of Sasanian Persia
w3_028.detail: Ardashir I overthrew the Parthians and founded the dynasty. It made Zoroastrianism the state religion and faced Rome across East and West.
w3_028.lesson: The tradition of an old empire became the legitimacy of a new dynasty.

w3_029.title: Council of Nicaea
w3_029.detail: Emperor Constantine gathered bishops from all regions to unify doctrine. The first case of an emperor presiding over a church council.
w3_029.lesson: Religious unity was tied to imperial unity.

w3_030.title: Founding of Constantinople
w3_030.detail: Emperor Constantine made Byzantium on the Bosporus the new capital. It would become the capital of the Eastern Empire for more than a thousand years.
w3_030.lesson: A position controlling trade routes decided a city's lifespan.

w3_031.title: Germanic Migrations
w3_031.detail: Goths pushed by the Huns flowed into Roman territory. Tribes set up kingdoms one after another within the empire.
w3_031.lesson: People pushed out like billiard balls changed the shape of states.

w3_032.title: Faxian's Journey to India
w3_032.detail: The Eastern Jin monk Faxian set out for India past sixty, seeking Buddhist texts, going by land and returning by sea. He wrote the Record of Buddhist Kingdoms.
w3_032.lesson: The desire to learn made roads across borders.

w3_033.title: Sack of Rome
w3_033.detail: The Visigothic king Alaric entered Rome and plundered it for three days. Rome falling to an outside enemy for the first time in about 800 years impressed upon people the empire's decline.
w3_033.lesson: The fall of a city believed impregnable shook people's hearts greatly.

w3_034.title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
w3_034.detail: A combined force of Romans and Visigoths and others defeated Attila of the Huns. The Huns' advance into Western Europe stopped.
w3_034.lesson: Before a common enemy, former enemies join hands.

w3_035.title: Conversion of Clovis
w3_035.detail: The Frankish king Clovis converted to Catholicism (the Athanasian creed). Gaining the support of the Roman population, he cemented the foundations of the Frankish kingdom.
w3_035.lesson: The choice of faith also became a tool for governing conquered land.

w3_036.title: Hagia Sophia
w3_036.detail: Emperor Justinian completed a great cathedral with a huge dome in only about five years. It later became a mosque and still stands.
w3_036.lesson: Architecture carves an empire's wealth, technology and faith into stone.

w3_037.title: Sui Reunify China
w3_037.detail: Ending about 300 years of division, Emperor Wen of Sui unified China. A forerunner of the examination system for hiring talent and, later, the Grand Canal advanced.
w3_037.lesson: The longer the division, the larger the work of building institutions after unification.

w3_038.title: Start of the Rashidun Caliphate
w3_038.detail: After the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr was chosen as first caliph. Expansion from Arabia into western Asia and Egypt was rapid.
w3_038.lesson: The faith community worked directly as the framework of a state.

w3_039.title: Islamic Advance into Iberia
w3_039.detail: Tariq of the Umayyads crossed from North Africa at Gibraltar and destroyed the Visigothic kingdom. For about 800 years afterward Islamic culture took root in Iberia.
w3_039.lesson: Where cultures meet, translation and trade arise.

w3_040.title: Founding of the Abbasid Caliphate
w3_040.detail: The Abbasids, who overthrew the Umayyads, granted equality even to non-Arab Muslims. Their capital Baghdad later flourished as the "City of Peace."
w3_040.lesson: Binding people by faith rather than origin expanded the empire.

w3_041.title: An Lushan Rebellion
w3_041.detail: The military governors An Lushan and Shi Siming rebelled against the Tang. Tang recovered, but military governors became autonomous and national strength greatly declined.
w3_041.lesson: Giving too much power to frontier armies shakes the center.

w3_042.title: Treaty of Verdun
w3_042.detail: Charlemagne's grandsons divided the empire in three. The division is regarded as the basis of later France, Germany and Italy.
w3_042.lesson: The division of an inheritance decided the shape of states.

w3_043.title: Oldest Printed Book: the Diamond Sutra
w3_043.detail: A woodblock-printed sutra found at Dunhuang carries a date in the ninth year of Xiantong (868). It is regarded as one of the world's oldest dated printed books.
w3_043.lesson: Reproduction technology was first used to spread words of prayer.

w3_044.title: Fall of the Tang
w3_044.detail: The military governor Zhu Quanzhong overthrew the Tang, and China entered the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms division.
w3_044.lesson: At the end of a strong dynasty, soldiers' power comes to the fore.

w3_045.title: Founding of the Song
w3_045.detail: The Later Zhou general Zhao Kuangyin founded the Song and set up a system in which civil officials control the army. The capital Kaifeng thrived on commerce.
w3_045.lesson: An age of warlords was settled by a civil-official system.

w3_046.title: Founding of the Holy Roman Empire
w3_046.detail: Otto I received the imperial crown from the pope. The "empire" lasted until 1806 but was in practice closer to a gathering of princes.
w3_046.lesson: Though the name remains, the substance changes greatly.

w3_047.title: Kievan Rus' Adopts Christianity
w3_047.detail: Vladimir I was baptized in connection with his marriage to a Byzantine princess and made Eastern Orthodoxy the state religion. It became a wellspring of Russian and Ukrainian culture.
w3_047.lesson: Conversion was also diplomacy tying a state to a great power.

w3_048.title: East–West Schism
w3_048.detail: The pope of Rome and the patriarch of Constantinople excommunicated each other, splitting into Catholic and Orthodox churches.
w3_048.lesson: Small doctrinal differences and a struggle for authority made a thousand-year gulf.

w3_049.title: Norman Conquest
w3_049.detail: William, Duke of Normandy, defeated King Harold of England at Hastings and took the throne. French words entered English in large numbers.
w3_049.lesson: Conquest remakes language and institutions for a long time.

w3_050.title: Walk to Canossa
w3_050.detail: Emperor Henry IV of the Holy Roman Empire begged Pope Gregory VII for forgiveness in the snow to have his excommunication lifted.
w3_050.lesson: A scene in which the balance of power between emperor and pope showed in an instant.

w3_051.title: Battle of Hattin
w3_051.detail: Saladin's Islamic army defeated the Crusaders and retook Jerusalem. He is also known for his leniency toward prisoners.
w3_051.lesson: A victor's generosity earned respect even from enemies.

w3_052.title: Sack of Constantinople in the Fourth Crusade
w3_052.detail: The crusade, used by Venice, attacked and plundered the capital of a fellow Christian state instead of the Holy Land and set up the "Latin Empire."
w3_052.lesson: When purpose is swapped for debts and business convenience, a movement's ideals are lost.

w3_053.title: Founding of the Mali Empire
w3_053.detail: Sundiata Keita defeated the Sosso kingdom at Kirina and built the Mali Empire in West Africa. It prospered on gold and salt trade.
w3_053.lesson: A state holding the trade routes can unite a wide region.

w3_054.title: Fall of Baghdad
w3_054.detail: Hulagu's Mongol army took Baghdad and destroyed the Abbasid Caliphate. Libraries and centers of learning suffered great damage.
w3_054.lesson: Even a city of learning falls easily once it loses its defenses.

w3_055.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
w3_055.detail: Egypt's Mamluk Sultanate defeated the Mongol army and stopped the Mongol westward advance.
w3_055.lesson: Even an army that seemed invincible could be stopped head-on.

w3_056.title: Yuan Dynasty Name
w3_056.detail: Kublai set the dynastic name "Great Yuan," calling his a Chinese-style dynasty. He later destroyed the Southern Song and ruled all China.
w3_056.lesson: A nomad empire began governing with Chinese institutions.

w3_057.title: Fall of Acre
w3_057.detail: The Mamluks took Acre, the Crusaders' last stronghold, and the Latin states of the Holy Land vanished.
w3_057.lesson: About 200 years of expeditions ended, leaving flows of Mediterranean trade and information.

w3_058.title: Avignon Papacy
w3_058.detail: Under the French king's influence, the papal court moved to Avignon in southern France. It lasted about 70 years and greatly damaged papal authority.
w3_058.lesson: A time when religious authority was nearly subordinated to secular power.

w3_059.title: Start of the Hundred Years' War
w3_059.detail: England's Edward III claimed the French throne and fighting began. It lasted about 116 years and nurtured national consciousness in both countries.
w3_059.lesson: A long war created the sense of being "English" and "French."

w3_060.title: Jacquerie
w3_060.detail: French peasants suffering from the Hundred Years' War and heavy taxes rose up but were crushed by the nobles.
w3_060.lesson: The burdens of war always fall on the weakest.

w3_061.title: Wat Tyler's Rebellion
w3_061.detail: English peasants opposed to the poll tax marched to London. Their leader was killed during negotiations, but the poll tax was abolished.
w3_061.lesson: Even if a revolt is put down, institutions can still be moved.

w3_062.title: Battle of Agincourt
w3_062.detail: Henry V's English army, aided by longbowmen, defeated a great host of French knights.
w3_062.lesson: A combination of weapons showed the end of the age of knights.

w3_063.title: Start of the Wars of the Roses
w3_063.detail: The houses of Lancaster and York fought over the throne until Henry Tudor's accession (1485). Their badges were the red rose and the white rose.
w3_063.lesson: Royal feuds cut down feudal nobles and opened the way to absolutism.

w3_064.title: Decline of Cahokia and Mississippian Culture
w3_064.detail: Cahokia, in present-day Illinois, flourished as a city of great earthen mounds, with perhaps 20,000 living there at its peak. It declined around the 14th century.
w3_064.lesson: North America too had large cities and trade networks.

w3_065.title: Fall of Granada
w3_065.detail: The Spanish monarchs took Granada, the Nasrid dynasty's last stronghold, completing the Reconquista. In the same year, Columbus set sail.
w3_065.lesson: The momentum of reconquest turned straight into overseas expansion.

w3_066.title: Treaty of Tordesillas
w3_066.detail: Spain and Portugal agreed to divide the world in two with a line across the Atlantic. The native peoples were not involved at all.
w3_066.lesson: A line on a map decided the fate of distant lands.

w3_067.title: Magellan's Circumnavigation
w3_067.detail: A fleet led by Magellan set out, and in 1522 one ship returned, completing a voyage around the world. Magellan himself died fighting in the Philippines.
w3_067.lesson: The voyage proved that the Earth is round and the seas are connected.

w3_068.title: Accession of Suleiman I
w3_068.detail: Suleiman I, who built the Ottoman Empire's peak, took the throne. He besieged Vienna and contended for supremacy in the Mediterranean.
w3_068.lesson: A strong monarch and strong bureaucrats led the empire to its golden age.

w3_069.title: Battle of Chaldiran
w3_069.detail: The Ottoman army defeated Safavid cavalry with muskets and cannon. A battle that showed the power of firearms.
w3_069.lesson: The side that adopted new weapons controlled the battlefield.

w3_070.title: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres
w3_070.detail: Copernicus published a book setting out the theory that the Earth moves around the Sun. Said to have been just before his death.

w3_071.title: Peace of Augsburg
w3_071.detail: In the Holy Roman Empire, Lutheranism was recognized—but on the principle that the ruler's denomination decides the subjects' (the ruler's religion is the region's).
w3_071.lesson: Freedom of faith was first granted as a prince's freedom.

w3_072.title: Battle of Lepanto
w3_072.detail: The combined fleet of Spain, Venice and the pope defeated the Ottoman fleet. The writer Cervantes also served.
w3_072.lesson: The last great sea battle between galleys.

w3_073.title: St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre
w3_073.detail: In Paris, Catholic crowds attacked Huguenots (Protestants) and thousands were killed. France's wars of religion grew fierce.
w3_073.lesson: Religious conflict, once used as a political tool, loses its brakes.

w3_074.title: Accession of Abbas I
w3_074.detail: He built the Safavid peak and founded the new capital Isfahan, which came to be called "half the world."
w3_074.lesson: A strong state shows itself with a beautiful city.

w3_075.title: Spanish Armada
w3_075.detail: The English navy defeated Spain's "Invincible Armada." Storms also helped. Supremacy in the Atlantic began to shift.
w3_075.lesson: The maneuverability of small ships toyed with a great fleet.

w3_076.title: Battle of Tondibi
w3_076.detail: A Moroccan army with muskets defeated the Songhai Empire and a West African power collapsed. The center of Saharan trade also shifted.
w3_076.lesson: The side with firearms broke up a vast territory at once.

w3_077.title: Edict of Nantes
w3_077.detail: Henry IV granted Protestants (Huguenots) freedom of worship. About 90 years later Louis XIV revoked it and many Protestants left the country.
w3_077.lesson: A country that abandons tolerance loses its technicians and merchants.

w3_078.title: Founding of Jamestown
w3_078.detail: England built its first permanent colony in North America. It later flourished on tobacco, and in 1619 Africans were brought there.
w3_078.lesson: A place called a land of freedom began together with slavery.

w3_079.title: Start of the Thirty Years' War
w3_079.detail: Starting from a Protestant revolt in Bohemia, a religious war that drew in European states. Germany's population fell greatly.
w3_079.lesson: The wars of religion eventually became wars of interest between states.

w3_080.title: Mayflower
w3_080.detail: A group of Puritans seeking freedom of worship landed at Plymouth in North America. Before landing they made the "Mayflower Compact."
w3_080.lesson: The experience of agreeing among themselves to build a society led to later American self-government.

w3_081.title: Construction of the Taj Mahal Begins
w3_081.detail: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan began building a white-marble mausoleum for his late consort. It took about 20 years.
w3_081.lesson: Love and power drove architecture to the height of beauty.

w3_082.title: Puritan Revolution
w3_082.detail: Civil war between King Charles I and Parliament began, and in 1649 the king was executed, leading to Cromwell's republic.
w3_082.lesson: The principle that even the king is under the law was confirmed in blood.

w3_083.title: Qing Enter the Pass
w3_083.detail: Li Zicheng's rebellion destroyed the Ming and Manchu Qing armies entered Beijing. The queue hairstyle was imposed on the Han too.
w3_083.lesson: A small number of conquerors ruled by inheriting China's institutions.

w3_084.title: Founding of the Cape Colony
w3_084.detail: The Dutch East India Company set up a supply base at Africa's southern tip. White settlement then continued to expand.
w3_084.lesson: A waystation on the sea route became the start of a long history of settlement and racism.

w3_085.title: Second Siege of Vienna
w3_085.detail: The Ottoman army besieged Vienna but was driven back by relief forces including King Sobieski of Poland. Afterward Ottoman territory began to shrink.
w3_085.lesson: The point of the attacker's furthest advance became the start of decline.

w3_086.title: Glorious Revolution
w3_086.detail: Parliament drove out James II and welcomed the Dutch stadtholder William. Almost bloodlessly, it led to the Bill of Rights (1689).
w3_086.lesson: That Parliament stands above the king was settled as an institution.

w3_087.title: Treaty of Nerchinsk
w3_087.detail: A treaty in which Qing and Russia fixed their border. Regarded as one of the first modern treaties Qing made as an equal state.
w3_087.lesson: Two expanding empires drew a boundary and faced each other.

w3_088.title: Founding of St. Petersburg
w3_088.detail: Peter the Great built a new capital on the marshes of the Neva. As a "window to the West," it became a symbol of Russia's modernization.
w3_088.lesson: Moving the capital was a declaration of changing the nation's direction.

w3_089.title: Seven Years' War
w3_089.detail: Britain and France fought in Europe, North America and India, and Britain decisively gained the upper hand in the colonies. Fiscal difficulties later led to heavier taxation of North America.
w3_089.lesson: Victory in a world-scale war became the spark of the next revolution.

w3_090.title: Battle of Plassey
w3_090.detail: The British East India Company's army defeated the combined forces of the Nawab of Bengal and France. It became a foothold for ruling India.
w3_090.lesson: A company's army turned into the ruler of a vast region.

w3_091.title: Watt's Steam Engine
w3_091.detail: James Watt patented a steam engine with greatly improved efficiency. It became the power for factories, mines and later railways.
w3_091.lesson: Power was freed from people and water wheels.

w3_092.title: The Wealth of Nations
w3_092.detail: Adam Smith set out the division of labor and the market's "invisible hand." Regarded as the starting point of modern economics.
w3_092.lesson: The idea that free exchange enriches society as a whole made the modern age.

w3_093.title: Execution of Louis XVI
w3_093.detail: During the French Revolution the king was guillotined. Europe's monarchies allied against the Revolution and war widened.
w3_093.lesson: The king's execution was a point of no return.

w3_094.title: Louisiana Purchase
w3_094.detail: America bought a vast area west of the Mississippi from Napoleon's France. The national territory roughly doubled at once.
w3_094.lesson: The land was bought and sold ignoring the presence of native peoples.

w3_095.title: Battle of Austerlitz
w3_095.detail: Napoleon defeated the Russian and Austrian armies. In the same year the British navy beat the Franco-Spanish fleet at Trafalgar, making an invasion of Britain impossible.
w3_095.lesson: Napoleon on land and Britain at sea each won a decisive victory.

w3_096.title: Napoleon's Russian Campaign
w3_096.detail: A great army of nearly 600,000 entered Moscow but retreated and was annihilated by scorched-earth tactics and the winter cold.
w3_096.lesson: A great army that lost its supply lost more to the climate than to the enemy.

w3_097.title: Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna
w3_097.detail: Napoleon was finally defeated. The Congress of Vienna built a conservative international system trying to restore the pre-Revolution order.
w3_097.lesson: A mechanism for keeping the balance of power supported about a hundred years without major war.

w3_098.title: World's First Steam Railway
w3_098.detail: Stephenson's locomotive began commercial service between Stockton and Darlington.
w3_098.lesson: The railway changed the sense of time and distance.

w3_099.title: July Revolution
w3_099.detail: Parisians rose up and forced Charles X of the Bourbons to abdicate. It influenced Belgian independence, the Polish uprising and elsewhere.

w3_100.title: Springtime of Nations
w3_100.detail: Beginning with France's February Revolution, liberal and nationalist movements rose at once in Vienna, Berlin, Hungary, Italy and elsewhere.
w3_100.lesson: The movements arose and mostly were suppressed—yet their demands were later realized.

w3_101.title: California Gold Rush
w3_101.detail: With the discovery of gold, people poured in from all over the world. San Francisco grew rapidly and native lives were destroyed.
w3_101.lesson: Migration chasing a dream rapidly changed the West.

w3_102.title: Great Exhibition in London
w3_102.detail: Industrial products from around the world were gathered in the giant glass Crystal Palace. It became a festival showing the results of the Industrial Revolution.
w3_102.lesson: Technological achievements became a showpiece of national power.

w3_103.title: Taiping Rebellion
w3_103.detail: Hong Xiuquan led the "God Worshippers' Society" in revolt and made Nanjing his capital. The Qing took over a decade to put it down; deaths are said to number in the tens of millions.
w3_103.lesson: A civil war joining religion and poverty produced casualties among the largest in history.

w3_104.title: Crimean War
w3_104.detail: Russia fought the Ottomans, Britain, France and others. Known for Nightingale's nursing, it was the start of modern war using the telegraph and railways.
w3_104.lesson: War reporting and nursing changed society's awareness.

w3_105.title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
w3_105.detail: A revolt by Indian soldiers (sepoys) of the East India Company spread across regions. After it was put down, the Company was dissolved and rule shifted to direct British government.
w3_105.lesson: Accumulated grievances exploded in a single event.

w3_106.title: Emancipation of Russian Serfs
w3_106.detail: Alexander II emancipated the serfs. The background was a strong recognition, after defeat in the Crimean War, of the need to modernize.
w3_106.lesson: Defeat in war becomes the greatest motive for reform.

w3_107.title: Emancipation Proclamation
w3_107.detail: Lincoln declared the freeing of slaves in the rebel Southern areas. The same year's Battle of Gettysburg was the Civil War's turning point, and in his address he called for government "of the people, by the people, for the people."
w3_107.lesson: The war's aim widened from preserving the Union to expanding freedom.

w3_108.title: Transcontinental Railroad Completed
w3_108.detail: America's eastern and western railroads were joined in Utah. Chinese immigrant workers also carried out construction.
w3_108.lesson: The railroad turned a vast land into one market.

w3_109.title: Founding of the German Empire
w3_109.detail: Amid the victory in the Franco-Prussian War, the king of Prussia was proclaimed German emperor at the Palace of Versailles.
w3_109.lesson: German unification was achieved by "iron and blood" and victory in war.

w3_110.title: Bell's Telephone
w3_110.detail: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone. Telephone exchange networks became infrastructure linking cities and firms.
w3_110.lesson: Technology carrying voices across distance made communication everyday.

w3_111.title: Eiffel Tower
w3_111.detail: An iron tower 300 m high was built for the Paris Exposition marking the Revolution's centennial. At the time there was criticism that it spoiled the view.
w3_111.lesson: A form born of new technology becomes a city's symbol as time passes.

w3_112.title: First Sino-Japanese War
w3_112.detail: Over control of Korea, Japan beat Qing. By the Treaty of Shimonoseki it gained Taiwan and more. The order in East Asia changed greatly.
w3_112.lesson: The weakness of the "sleeping lion" accelerated the Powers' carving up of China.

w3_113.title: Spanish–American War
w3_113.detail: Under the name of supporting Cuba's independence movement, America fought and beat Spain. It gained the Philippines, Guam and Puerto Rico and expanded overseas.
w3_113.lesson: America stepped onto the path of "empire."

w3_114.title: Second Boer War
w3_114.detail: Over South Africa's gold and diamonds, Britain fought the Boers (of Dutch descent). The many deaths in camps drew criticism.
w3_114.lesson: A war over resources left a precedent for modern concentration camps.

w3_115.title: Boxer Rebellion
w3_115.detail: The Boxers, under the banner "support the Qing, destroy the foreigners," besieged the foreign legations in Beijing. An eight-nation alliance put it down and Qing bore huge indemnities.
w3_115.lesson: Even as resentment of foreigners grew, the Powers' control rather strengthened.

w3_116.title: Wright Brothers' First Flight
w3_116.detail: They succeeded in powered, piloted flight in North Carolina. The first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered about 36 m.
w3_116.lesson: A small experiment changed 20th-century war and transport.

w3_117.title: Russo-Japanese War
w3_117.detail: At the Battle of Tsushima, Japan defeated Russia's Baltic Fleet and made peace by the Treaty of Portsmouth. An Asian country beating a European great power influenced national movements in many places.
w3_117.lesson: An Asian victory gave courage to colonized peoples.

w3_118.title: Bloody Sunday
w3_118.detail: In St. Petersburg, the army fired on people petitioning peacefully. It triggered the first Russian Revolution.
w3_118.lesson: Trust in "the tsar as father of the people" collapsed in a day.

w3_119.title: Ford Model T
w3_119.detail: Henry Ford mass-produced automobiles on an assembly line and cut prices greatly. The car became a vehicle for the masses.
w3_119.lesson: An innovation in production methods changed life and changed society.

w3_120.title: Opening of the Panama Canal
w3_120.detail: A canal linking the Pacific and Atlantic was completed. Built under American leadership, it changed world shipping.
w3_120.lesson: Works that remake terrain also cost enormous human lives.

w3_121.title: Battles of Verdun and the Somme
w3_121.detail: On World War I's Western Front, wars of attrition with hundreds of thousands of casualties. At the Somme tanks were used for the first time.
w3_121.lesson: Advances in weapons multiplied losses of life by orders of magnitude.

w3_122.title: Spanish Flu
w3_122.detail: A new influenza that spread in the last stage of World War I. Tens of millions died worldwide. Because of wartime press control, it was named for neutral Spain.
w3_122.lesson: Infectious disease crossed borders along with war.

w3_123.title: Treaty of Versailles
w3_123.detail: The peace treaty of World War I. Germany lost part of its territory and bore huge reparations. The League of Nations was also founded.
w3_123.lesson: A harsh peace left the spark of the next war.

w3_124.title: May Fourth Movement
w3_124.detail: Students in Beijing protested on learning that the Paris Peace Conference gave Shandong's former German rights to Japan. A turning point for China's national movement.

w3_125.title: March on Rome
w3_125.detail: It became the occasion for Mussolini's Fascist Party to take power. The world's first fascist government, later a model for Hitler.
w3_125.lesson: Dictatorship is born in the gaps of parliamentary politics.

w3_126.title: Founding of the Republic of Turkey
w3_126.detail: Kemal Atatürk abolished the Ottoman sultanate and established a republic. He pushed separation of religion and state and alphabet reform.
w3_126.lesson: Modernization from above changed the shape of the nation in a short time.

w3_127.title: The Long March
w3_127.detail: The Communist army, pursued by Nationalist forces, traveled about 12,000 km from Jiangxi to Shaanxi. Mao Zedong consolidated his leadership.
w3_127.lesson: A retreat became the legend of a later victory.

w3_128.title: Spanish Civil War
w3_128.detail: The Republican government fought General Franco's rebel army. Germany and Italy backed Franco and the USSR the Republic, and the bombing of Guernica occurred.
w3_128.lesson: As a prelude to World War II, the powers tested their forces.

w3_129.title: Second Sino-Japanese War
w3_129.detail: Triggered by the Marco Polo Bridge Incident, Japan and China entered full-scale war. Nanjing fell and the fighting dragged on.
w3_129.lesson: A war with no end in sight led into a world war.

w3_130.title: Battle of Britain
w3_130.detail: The German air force tried to seize air superiority over Britain, but radar and fighter squadrons held it off. Hitler's plan to invade Britain was abandoned.
w3_130.lesson: Technology and organization overturned a difference in numbers.

w3_131.title: German–Soviet War
w3_131.detail: The war began with Germany's invasion of the USSR. Tens of millions died on both sides. It became the largest fighting on the European front.
w3_131.lesson: A war with enormous sacrifice decided Germany's defeat.

w3_132.title: Battle of Stalingrad
w3_132.detail: Soviet forces encircled and forced the surrender of Germany's Sixth Army. It was the turning point of the German–Soviet War.
w3_132.lesson: The attrition of street fighting pushed the attacker to its limit.

w3_133.title: Normandy Landings
w3_133.detail: Allied forces landed on France's northern coast and opened the Western Front. Regarded as the largest amphibious operation in history.
w3_133.lesson: Preparation and supply made a decisive day.

w3_134.title: Founding of the United Nations
w3_134.detail: The UN Charter was adopted at the San Francisco Conference. Permanent members were given a veto.
w3_134.lesson: A mechanism to prevent renewed war was realized in exchange for the great powers' veto.

w3_135.title: Founding of Israel
w3_135.detail: After the UN partition plan for Palestine, Israel declared its founding. The first Arab–Israeli war followed and many Palestinians left their homes.
w3_135.lesson: One event became separate memories for two peoples.

w3_136.title: Founding of NATO
w3_136.detail: The US and Western European states formed the North Atlantic Treaty Organization for collective defense. The Soviet bloc countered with the Warsaw Pact (1955).
w3_136.lesson: A military alliance fixed the structure of the Cold War.

w3_137.title: DNA Double Helix
w3_137.detail: Watson and Crick showed the double-helix structure of DNA. Rosalind Franklin's X-ray photograph was an important clue.
w3_137.lesson: The shape of life's blueprint came into view and molecular biology began.

w3_138.title: Sputnik 1
w3_138.detail: The USSR launched the world's first artificial satellite. It shocked America and the space race began in earnest.
w3_138.lesson: A small metal sphere changed science education and military competition.

w3_139.title: Great Leap Forward
w3_139.detail: Mao Zedong aimed for rapid increases in agriculture and industry, but policy that ignored reality caused a massive famine.
w3_139.lesson: A politics of competing in numbers produces policies blind to reality.

w3_140.title: Cuban Revolution
w3_140.detail: Castro and others overthrew the Batista regime. It later drew close to the USSR, leading to the Cuban Missile Crisis.
w3_140.lesson: A revolution in a great neighbor's backyard became a front line of the Cold War.

w3_141.title: Building of the Berlin Wall
w3_141.detail: East Germany closed the boundary between East and West Berlin with a wall. Many citizens tried to flee and were killed.
w3_141.lesson: The wall was built to hide the regime's weakness.

w3_142.title: Gagarin's Spaceflight
w3_142.detail: The Soviet Yuri Gagarin made the first human spaceflight. Known for the words "The Earth is blue."
w3_142.lesson: Humanity saw the Earth from outside for the first time.

w3_143.title: Cultural Revolution
w3_143.detail: At Mao Zedong's call, Red Guards held denunciation campaigns everywhere, and intellectuals and cadres were persecuted. Society was in turmoil for ten years.
w3_143.lesson: A fervent movement deeply wounded culture and people.

w3_144.title: Six-Day War
w3_144.detail: Israel beat Egypt, Syria and Jordan in six days and occupied the Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank and the Golan Heights.
w3_144.lesson: A short war produced problems that continue today.

w3_145.title: May 1968 and the Prague Spring
w3_145.detail: In Paris students and workers protested; in Czechoslovakia "socialism with a human face" was tried and ended with Soviet intervention.
w3_145.lesson: In the same year, different demands for freedom arose in East and West.

w3_146.title: Bangladesh Independence
w3_146.detail: East Pakistan declared independence from Pakistan and, through Indian intervention, became independent.
w3_146.lesson: Differences of language and ethnicity led to the split of a state.

w3_147.title: Fall of Saigon
w3_147.detail: North Vietnamese forces entered Saigon, South Vietnam's capital, and the Vietnam War ended.
w3_147.lesson: A war from which a superpower withdrew left deep wounds in American society.

w3_148.title: Iranian Revolution
w3_148.detail: The Shah Pahlavi regime fell and an Islamic republic led by Khomeini was founded. The map of power in the Middle East changed.
w3_148.lesson: A regime that hurried modernization was toppled by a religious popular movement.

w3_149.title: Chernobyl Disaster
w3_149.detail: An explosion at a Soviet nuclear plant spread radioactive material across Europe. It became an occasion for demands for openness (glasnost).
w3_149.lesson: Covering up the accident shattered trust in the political system.

w3_150.title: Tiananmen Square Incident
w3_150.detail: The democracy movement of students and citizens gathered at Tiananmen Square in Beijing was suppressed by the army.
w3_150.lesson: In the very year Eastern Europe changed, China chose a different path.

w3_151.title: German Reunification
w3_151.detail: About a year after the fall of the Berlin Wall, East and West Germany were unified.
w3_151.lesson: The end of the Cold War redrew border lines.

w3_152.title: Gulf War
w3_152.detail: In response to Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, a US-led multinational force attacked. War was broadcast on television in real time.
w3_152.lesson: An age came when war was consumed as images.

w3_153.title: Founding of the EU
w3_153.detail: The Maastricht Treaty took effect and the European Community grew into the EU. In 2002 euro notes and coins went into circulation.
w3_153.lesson: Countries that once fought shared part of their sovereignty.

w3_154.title: South Africa's First All-Race Election
w3_154.detail: In the first election with all races taking part, Mandela was chosen president and apartheid legally ended.
w3_154.lesson: The path of a "Truth and Reconciliation Commission" was chosen over revenge.

w3_155.title: Asian Financial Crisis
w3_155.detail: From the plunge of the Thai baht, currency crises spread to South Korea, Indonesia and elsewhere.
w3_155.lesson: A sudden outflow of short-term capital shook growing economies at once.

w3_156.title: Handover of Hong Kong
w3_156.detail: Hong Kong was returned from Britain to China and "one country, two systems" began.
w3_156.lesson: A promise with a deadline changes meaning with time.

w3_157.title: Iraq War
w3_157.detail: US and British forces attacked Iraq on the grounds of its holding weapons of mass destruction and toppled Hussein's regime. No weapons were found.
w3_157.lesson: When the basis for going to war collapses, the war's legitimacy is questioned continually.

w3_158.title: Arab Spring
w3_158.detail: From a young Tunisian's protest, democracy movements spread to Egypt, Libya and elsewhere in the Middle East and North Africa. Social media played a role, but results differed greatly by country.
w3_158.lesson: The movements spread, but the difficulty of building a new order was great.

w3_159.title: Brexit Referendum
w3_159.detail: In a referendum, a majority voted to leave the EU, and Britain left in 2020.
w3_159.lesson: A direct vote reduced a complex question to two choices.

w3_160.title: COVID-19 Pandemic
w3_160.detail: The novel coronavirus spread worldwide, and lockdowns and remote work became common. Vaccines were also developed in an extremely short time.
w3_160.lesson: The world learned it could be stopped all at once by a single infectious disease.

w4_001.title: Homeric Epics
w4_001.detail: The Iliad and the Odyssey were handed down and later written down. They became a shared story for the Greeks.

w4_002.title: Solon's Reforms
w4_002.detail: In Athens, enslavement for debt was banned and political rights were divided by property. A step toward democracy.

w4_003.title: Cleisthenes' Reforms
w4_003.detail: Athenian citizens were reorganized into ten tribes and ostracism was set up. It laid the foundation of democracy.

w4_004.title: Parthenon
w4_004.detail: In Pericles' time, a temple to the goddess Athena was built on Athens' Acropolis.

w4_005.title: Death of Socrates
w4_005.detail: Socrates, who taught "knowing that you do not know," was sentenced to death at trial and drank the poison cup.

w4_006.title: Plato's Academy
w4_006.detail: A school opened on Athens' outskirts, regarded as Europe's oldest institution of higher learning.

w4_007.title: Battle of Chaeronea
w4_007.detail: Philip II of Macedon defeated the Greek allied army, and the age of the polis moved toward its end.

w4_008.title: Death of Alexander the Great
w4_008.detail: He died suddenly in Babylon, and the empire split among his successors (the Diadochi), who fought.

w4_009.title: Building of the Appian Way
w4_009.detail: The first full-scale paved road extending south from Rome. It became the prototype of the later Roman road network.

w4_010.title: Hortensian Law
w4_010.detail: Decisions of the plebeian assembly became law of the state, and the struggle of the orders between patricians and plebeians largely ended.

w4_011.title: Hannibal Crosses the Alps
w4_011.detail: The Carthaginian general crossed the Alps with elephants and attacked Rome.

w4_012.title: Battle of Cannae
w4_012.detail: Hannibal dealt Rome's army a devastating blow by encirclement. A classic of tactics.

w4_013.title: Destruction of Corinth
w4_013.detail: Rome destroyed Corinth and Greece was absorbed into the province of Macedonia.

w4_014.title: Marian Military Reforms
w4_014.detail: A system was made to hire propertyless citizens as volunteer soldiers. It was the start of soldiers becoming a general's private army.

w4_015.title: Caesar's Gallic Campaign
w4_015.detail: Over eight years he conquered present-day France. His record is the Gallic War.

w4_016.title: Crossing the Rubicon
w4_016.detail: "The die is cast." Caesar crossed leading his army, and civil war began.

w4_017.title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
w4_017.detail: Germanic tribes annihilated three Roman legions and the Rhine became Rome's boundary.

w4_018.title: Death of Augustus
w4_018.detail: The first emperor died. The framework of the Roman Empire was made by this man.

w4_019.title: Roman Conquest of Britain
w4_019.detail: Emperor Claudius conquered Britain and Londinium (London) was founded.

w4_020.title: Completion of the Colosseum
w4_020.detail: An amphitheater holding 50,000 was completed. Gladiatorial contests and more were held there.

w4_021.title: Hadrian's Wall
w4_021.detail: A stone barrier built across northern Britain. It remains today as a marker of the empire's frontier.

w4_022.title: Emperor Marcus Aurelius
w4_022.detail: The philosopher-emperor wrote his Meditations in camp during campaigns. The last of the Five Good Emperors.

w4_023.title: Caracalla Grants Citizenship
w4_023.detail: He gave Roman citizenship to free people in the empire, and the difference between Romans and others faded.

w4_024.title: Age of the Soldier Emperors
w4_024.detail: In about 50 years, emperors set up by the army replaced one another in turn, and the empire fell into civil war and chaos.

w4_025.title: Accession of Diocletian
w4_025.detail: He began the Tetrarchy, ruling the empire among four, and rebuilt administration and the army.

w4_026.title: Christianity Becomes the State Religion
w4_026.detail: Emperor Theodosius banned religions other than Christianity and made it the state religion.

w4_027.title: Vandal Sack of Rome
w4_027.detail: The Vandals, who had built a kingdom in North Africa, plundered Rome for two weeks.

w4_028.title: Monte Cassino Abbey
w4_028.detail: A monastery opened by Benedict. The rule "pray and work" became a model for monasteries.

w4_029.title: Corpus Juris Civilis
w4_029.detail: The compendium of Roman law compiled under Emperor Justinian. It later became the foundation of European law.

w4_030.title: Lombard Kingdom
w4_030.detail: A Germanic people advanced into northern Italy and built a kingdom.

w4_031.title: Archbishop of Canterbury
w4_031.detail: Augustine, an envoy of Pope Gregory I, began missionary work in England.

w4_032.title: Synod of Whitby
w4_032.detail: It debated whether to follow Roman or Irish custom, and England chose the Roman.

w4_033.title: Founding of the Carolingian Dynasty
w4_033.detail: Pepin took the throne with the pope's support. He later donated territory to the pope (756).

w4_034.title: Viking Raids
w4_034.detail: Northern sea peoples attacked Lindisfarne monastery in England. Afterward they raided all over Europe.

w4_035.title: Alfred the Great
w4_035.detail: He resisted Danish invasions, defended Wessex and laid the groundwork for England's unification.

w4_036.title: Duchy of Normandy
w4_036.detail: The Viking chief Rollo was given land by the West Frankish king.

w4_037.title: Battle of Lechfeld
w4_037.detail: Otto I defeated the Magyars and drove off the threat from the east.

w4_038.title: Founding of the Capetian Dynasty
w4_038.detail: Hugh Capet, Count of Paris, became king, starting the French royal house that lasted about 800 years.

w4_039.title: University of Bologna
w4_039.detail: Regarded as Europe's oldest university, known for law. It began from student guilds.

w4_040.title: Concordat of Worms
w4_040.detail: The dispute between pope and emperor over investiture of clergy was settled by compromise.

w4_041.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral
w4_041.detail: A masterpiece of Gothic architecture begun in Paris. Completion took about 200 years.

w4_042.title: Murder of Becket
w4_042.detail: Thomas Becket, Archbishop of Canterbury, was murdered after conflict with royal power.

w4_043.title: Albigensian Crusade
w4_043.detail: The pope attacked the heretical Cathars of southern France with a crusade.

w4_044.title: Battle of Legnica
w4_044.detail: The Mongol army defeated a Polish–German force but withdrew on news of the Great Khan's death.

w4_045.title: Origins of Parliament
w4_045.detail: Simon de Montfort convened a parliament inviting representatives of towns and shires.

w4_046.title: Rise of the Habsburgs
w4_046.detail: Rudolf I was chosen Holy Roman Emperor, and the family later ruled Austria as a leading house of Central Europe.

w4_047.title: Thomas Aquinas
