w4_047.detail: In the Summa Theologica, he tried to harmonize Christian faith with Aristotle's philosophy.

w4_048.title: Estates General
w4_048.detail: Philip IV of France invited representatives of clergy, nobles and commoners, amid conflict with the pope.

w4_049.title: Battle of Bannockburn
w4_049.detail: Scotland beat the English army and secured its independence.

w4_050.title: Dante's Divine Comedy
w4_050.detail: An epic Dante wrote in Italian, depicting a journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise.

w4_051.title: Boccaccio's Decameron
w4_051.detail: Men and women fleeing the Black Death tell 100 stories over ten days.

w4_052.title: Western Schism
w4_052.detail: Two popes arose at Rome and Avignon, and the Church's authority was damaged.

w4_053.title: Execution of Joan of Arc
w4_053.detail: In the Hundred Years' War, the girl who had liberated Orléans was burned at the stake in Rouen.

w4_054.title: Medici Rule
w4_054.detail: The Florentine banker Cosimo took real power and, patronizing art, supported the Renaissance.

w4_055.title: Battle of Bosworth
w4_055.detail: The Wars of the Roses were settled; Henry Tudor became king and the Tudor dynasty began.

w4_056.title: Mona Lisa
w4_056.detail: A portrait Leonardo da Vinci began painting. He is said to have kept working on it by his side for years.

w4_058.title: The Prince
w4_058.detail: Machiavelli discussed politics realistically, separated from morality.

w4_059.title: Thomas More's Utopia
w4_059.detail: Depicting an ideal island, it satirized English society of the time.

w4_060.title: Diet of Worms
w4_060.detail: Luther refused before the emperor to retract his views and was placed outside the protection of the law.

w4_061.title: German Peasants' War
w4_061.detail: Peasants inspired by the Reformation rose up, but Luther too backed the princes and it was crushed.

w4_062.title: Church of England
w4_062.detail: Henry VIII broke with the Roman Church over his divorce and made himself its head.

w4_063.title: Calvin's Institutes
w4_063.detail: Calvin, known for predestination, advanced reform in Geneva.

w4_064.title: Council of Trent
w4_064.detail: The Catholic Church reaffirmed its doctrine and institutions in response to the Reformation.

w4_065.title: Outbreak of the French Wars of Religion
w4_065.detail: In France, Catholics and Protestants (Huguenots) fought for about 30 years.

w4_066.title: Dutch Declaration of Independence
w4_066.detail: It declared independence from Spain and later led the world in commercial prosperity.

w4_067.title: Hamlet
w4_067.detail: Shakespeare completed his four great tragedies around 1600.

w4_068.title: Galileo's Telescope
w4_068.detail: With a telescope he observed lunar craters and Jupiter's moons and supported the heliocentric theory.

w4_069.title: Descartes' Discourse on Method
w4_069.detail: "I think, therefore I am." The starting point of modern philosophy.

w4_070.title: Execution of Charles I
w4_070.detail: The king was publicly executed and England became a republic.

w4_071.title: Restoration of the Monarchy
w4_071.detail: After Cromwell's death, Charles II took the throne and the monarchy returned.

w4_072.title: Great Fire of London
w4_072.detail: It burned for four days and destroyed most of the old city, which was later reborn as a city of stone.

w4_073.title: Move to Versailles
w4_073.detail: Louis XIV moved the court, gathered the nobles there and established absolutism.

w4_074.title: Revocation of the Edict of Nantes
w4_074.detail: Tolerance of the Huguenots was ended and about 200,000 fled the country.

w4_076.title: Russian Empire Proclaimed
w4_076.detail: Peter the Great took the title of emperor and led Russia into a modern state.

w4_077.title: War of the Austrian Succession
w4_077.detail: Objections to Maria Theresa's succession drew in all of Europe.

w4_078.title: Rousseau's Social Contract
w4_078.detail: "Man is born free." He taught that sovereignty lies with the people.

w4_079.title: Spinning Jenny
w4_079.detail: The multi-spindle spinning machine invented by Hargreaves advanced the mechanization of the cotton industry.

w4_080.title: First Partition of Poland
w4_080.detail: Russia, Prussia and Austria divided Poland's territory among themselves.

w4_081.title: Declaration of the Rights of Man
w4_081.detail: It proclaimed that "men are born and remain free and equal in rights."

w4_082.title: Coup of 18 Brumaire
w4_082.detail: Napoleon seized power by coup and the age of revolution ended.

w4_083.title: British Abolition of the Slave Trade
w4_083.detail: Parliament decided to ban the slave trade, the fruit of the persistent campaign of Wilberforce and others.

w4_084.title: Greek War of Independence
w4_084.detail: The Greeks rose against the Ottoman Empire and later won independence.

w4_085.title: First Reform Act
w4_085.detail: Seats were given to industrial cities and middle-class suffrage widened.

w4_086.title: Factory Act
w4_086.detail: It set limits on child labor, a first step in protecting workers.

w4_087.title: Accession of Queen Victoria
w4_087.detail: A 64-year reign that was the peak of the British Empire.

w4_088.title: On the Origin of Species
w4_088.detail: Darwin presented evolution by natural selection.

w4_089.title: Kingdom of Italy Founded
w4_089.detail: Italy was unified through the efforts of Garibaldi and Cavour.

w4_090.title: Marx's Das Kapital
w4_090.detail: It analyzed the workings of capitalism and greatly influenced the socialist movement.

w4_092.title: Paris Commune
w4_092.detail: The people of Paris built a self-governing regime for about two months but it was crushed.

w4_093.title: First Modern Olympics
w4_093.detail: Held in Athens at Coubertin's initiative.

w4_094.title: Einstein's Miracle Year
w4_094.detail: He published papers on special relativity and the light quantum hypothesis within one year.

w4_095.title: Sinking of the Titanic
w4_095.detail: It struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic and about 1,500 people died.

w4_096.title: Sarajevo Incident
w4_096.detail: The Austrian archduke and his wife were assassinated, triggering World War I.

w4_097.title: German Revolution
w4_097.detail: From a sailors' mutiny the emperor abdicated and a republic arose.

w4_098.title: Weimar Constitution
w4_098.detail: A constitution said to be the most democratic in the world at the time. It was the first to state social rights explicitly.

w4_099.title: Beer Hall Putsch
w4_099.detail: The coup Hitler launched failed but made his name known.

w4_100.title: Munich Agreement
w4_100.detail: Britain and France pursued appeasement, having part of Czechoslovakia ceded to Germany.

w4_101.title: Yalta Conference
w4_101.detail: The leaders of the US, Britain and the USSR discussed the postwar settlement.

w4_102.title: "Iron Curtain" Speech
w4_102.detail: Churchill said Europe had been divided into East and West.

w4_103.title: Berlin Blockade
w4_103.detail: The USSR blocked land routes to West Berlin, and the West kept sending supplies by airlift.

w4_104.title: European Coal and Steel Community
w4_104.detail: France and Germany jointly managed the resources that caused war. The origin of the EU.

w4_105.title: Hungarian Uprising
w4_105.detail: A popular uprising was crushed by Soviet troops.

w4_106.title: Thatcher Becomes Prime Minister
w4_106.detail: Called the "Iron Lady," she pushed privatization and deregulation.

w4_107.title: Rise of Gorbachev
w4_107.detail: Becoming general secretary, he pursued perestroika (reform) and glasnost (openness).

w4_108.title: Euro Notes and Coins Enter Circulation
w4_108.detail: The euro began to be used in 12 countries at once.

w4_109.title: EU Eastern Enlargement
w4_109.detail: Ten countries, including Eastern European ones, joined at once.

w4_110.title: European Refugee Crisis
w4_110.detail: Because of the Syrian civil war and other causes, over a million refugees reached Europe.

w4_111.title: Akkadian Empire
w4_111.detail: Sargon I is said to have unified Mesopotamia and created the first empire.

w4_112.title: Aryan Migration into India
w4_112.detail: Aryans who settled in northwest India created the Vedic religion and the origins of the caste system.

w4_113.title: Composition of the Vedas
w4_113.detail: The sacred texts of Brahmanism. Hymns to the gods and rituals were passed down orally.

w4_114.title: Laozi and Daoism
w4_114.detail: Laozi is said to have taught a natural way following the "Dao." Whether he existed is debated.

w4_115.title: Cyrus II's Conquest of Babylon
w4_115.detail: Cyrus of the Achaemenids conquered Babylon and freed the Jews.

w4_116.title: Accession of Darius I
w4_116.detail: He set up the satrapy system and the "Royal Road," and the Achaemenids reached their peak.

w4_117.title: Start of the Warring States Period
w4_117.detail: Jin split into three states and China became an age of seven contending states.

w4_118.title: Shang Yang's Reforms
w4_118.detail: Rule by law was strengthened in Qin. It later became the base of Qin's unification.

w4_119.title: Founding of the Maurya Dynasty
w4_119.detail: Chandragupta built India's first unified dynasty.

w4_120.title: Kalinga War
w4_120.detail: Seeing the carnage of war, Ashoka turned to Buddhism and sought rule by Dharma.

w4_121.title: Accession of Emperor Wu
w4_121.detail: Emperor Wu of Han launched campaigns against the Xiongnu and made Confucianism the official learning, leading Han to its peak.

w4_122.title: Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian
w4_122.detail: He wrote a history in the annals-biography form, a model for Chinese histories.

w4_123.title: Founding of the Xin Dynasty
w4_123.detail: Wang Mang overthrew the Han and founded Xin, but idealistic reforms brought chaos.

w4_125.title: Buddhism Reaches China
w4_125.detail: In the reign of Emperor Ming of Later Han, monks are said to have come from India and the White Horse Temple was built in Luoyang.

w4_126.title: King Kanishka
w4_126.detail: A king at the Kushan peak who protected Buddhism. Mahayana Buddhism spread.

w4_127.title: Three Kingdoms of Wei, Wu and Shu
w4_127.detail: The Later Han fell and an age of three contending states began.

w4_128.title: Jin Unifies China
w4_128.detail: The Western Jin destroyed Wu and unified China but soon collapsed in civil strife.

w4_129.title: Sixteen Kingdoms of the Five Barbarians
w4_129.detail: Nomadic states rose and fell one after another in North China.

w4_130.title: Founding of the Gupta Dynasty
w4_130.detail: It unified northern India, and Sanskrit literature and mathematics developed.

w4_131.title: Founding of the Northern Wei
w4_131.detail: A state built in North China by the Xianbei Tuoba clan. It later pursued Sinicization.

w4_132.title: Equal-Field System
w4_132.detail: In the Northern Wei, a system began in which the state gave land to peasants. It was later carried on by the Sui and Tang.

w4_133.title: Longmen Grottoes
w4_133.detail: Buddhist remains the Northern Wei began building near Luoyang. Great Buddhas stand in rows.

w4_134.title: Rise of the Turks
w4_134.detail: A nomadic state formed on the Mongolian plateau and greatly influenced East–West trade.

w4_135.title: Birth of Muhammad
w4_135.detail: Born in Mecca, he is said to have received divine revelation at about age 40.

w4_136.title: Building of the Grand Canal
w4_136.detail: Emperor Yang of Sui opened a canal linking the Yellow and Yangtze Rivers, unifying the flow of goods between north and south.

w4_137.title: Xuanzang's Journey to India
w4_137.detail: The Tang monk Xuanzang traveled to India seeking Buddhist texts and later left the Great Tang Records on the Western Regions.

w4_138.title: Fall of the Sasanian Empire
w4_138.detail: Defeated by Islamic forces, the Sasanians fell and the Islamization of Iran advanced.

w4_139.title: Accession of Empress Wu Zetian
w4_139.detail: The consort of Tang's Gaozong founded "Zhou" as China's only female emperor.

w4_140.title: Founding of Baghdad
w4_140.detail: A round city built by the Abbasid al-Mansur. It became the center of the world's commerce and learning.

w4_141.title: Harun al-Rashid
w4_141.detail: The caliph at the Abbasid peak. He also appears in the One Thousand and One Nights.

w4_142.title: Founding of the Liao (Khitan)
w4_142.detail: Yelü Abaoji ruled from the Mongolian plateau to northern North China.

w4_143.title: Treaty of Chanyuan
w4_143.detail: Song made peace with Liao by promising yearly silver and silk.

w4_144.title: Founding of Western Xia
w4_144.detail: A state the Tangut built in the northwest. It created its own Western Xia script.

w4_145.title: Wang Anshi's New Policies
w4_145.detail: To rebuild Song finances he enacted measures such as the Green Sprouts Law but clashed with conservatives.

w4_146.title: Founding of the Jin
w4_146.detail: Founded by the Jurchen Wanyan Aguda, it later destroyed the Liao.

w4_147.title: Jingkang Incident
w4_147.detail: Jin forces took the Song capital Kaifeng and carried off the emperor. Song moved south and became the Southern Song.

w4_148.title: Genghis Khan's Western Campaign
w4_148.detail: He attacked the Khwarazmian Empire and conquered Central Asia.

w4_149.title: Death of Genghis Khan
w4_149.detail: He died during a campaign against Western Xia. The empire was divided among his descendants.

w4_150.title: Fall of the Jin
w4_150.detail: A Mongol–Southern Song alliance destroyed the Jin.

w4_151.title: Fall of the Southern Song
w4_151.detail: The Southern Song fell at the Battle of Yamen and the Yuan ruled all China.

w4_152.title: Vijayanagara Kingdom
w4_152.detail: A kingdom built by Hindus in southern India. It resisted Islamic powers.

w4_153.title: Red Turban Rebellion
w4_153.detail: Revolts by White Lotus followers and others spread and triggered the Yuan's collapse.

w4_154.title: Timurid Dynasty
w4_154.detail: Timur made Samarkand his capital and built a great empire in Central Asia.

w4_155.title: Battle of Ankara
w4_155.detail: Timur defeated Bayezid I of the Ottoman Empire.

w4_156.title: Move of the Capital to Beijing
w4_156.detail: The Yongle Emperor moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing and built the Forbidden City.

w4_157.title: Tumu Crisis
w4_157.detail: The Ming emperor was captured by the Mongol Oirats.

w4_158.title: Safavid Dynasty
w4_158.detail: Founded in Iran by Ismail I, with Shia Islam as the state religion.

w4_159.title: Portuguese Capture of Malacca
w4_159.detail: Seizing a key point of the spice trade, it became a foothold into Southeast Asia.

w4_160.title: Accession of Akbar the Great
w4_160.detail: Akbar of the Mughal Empire sought harmony with Hindus and stabilized the empire.

w4_161.title: Imjin War
w4_161.detail: Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasion of Korea. In Korea, Yi Sun-sin's navy distinguished itself.

w4_162.title: Founding of the Later Jin
w4_162.detail: Nurhaci unified the Jurchens and founded it. It later developed into the Qing.

w4_163.title: Koxinga Takes Taiwan
w4_163.detail: He drove out the Dutch and built a base in Taiwan.

w4_164.title: Qing Rule of Taiwan
w4_164.detail: The Zheng regime was made to surrender and Taiwan came under Qing rule.

w4_165.title: Nader Shah's Sack of Delhi
w4_165.detail: Iranian forces plundered the Mughal capital and the empire's decline became decisive.

w4_166.title: Macartney Mission to China
w4_166.detail: A British envoy sought expanded trade but was refused by the Qianlong Emperor.

w4_167.title: Treaty of Nanjing
w4_167.detail: In the peace treaty of the Opium War, Qing agreed to cede Hong Kong Island and open Shanghai and other ports.

w4_168.title: Second Opium War (Arrow War)
w4_168.detail: Britain and France attacked Qing, and the Convention of Beijing (1860) allowed open ports and foreign legations in Beijing.

w4_169.title: Indian National Congress
w4_169.detail: A political organization formed in British-ruled India. It later became the center of the independence movement.

w4_170.title: Hundred Days' Reform
w4_170.detail: The modernization reforms of the Guangxu Emperor and Kang Youwei were crushed in a little over a hundred days by Empress Dowager Cixi.

w4_171.title: Founding of the Republic of China
w4_171.detail: Sun Yat-sen became provisional president and Asia's first republic was founded.

w4_172.title: Founding of the Chinese Communist Party
w4_172.detail: The first congress was held in Shanghai.

w4_173.title: Start of the Northern Expedition
w4_173.detail: The National Revolutionary Army led by Chiang Kai-shek sought to unify China by defeating the warlords.

w4_174.title: Nanjing Incident
w4_174.detail: When Japanese forces occupied Nanjing, many Chinese were killed.

w4_175.title: Founding of the Republic of Korea and the DPRK
w4_175.detail: The Korean Peninsula split into two states along the 38th parallel.

w4_176.title: Korean War Armistice
w4_176.detail: An armistice agreement was signed at Panmunjom. No peace treaty has been concluded.

w4_177.title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
w4_177.detail: Vietnamese forces defeated the French, and France withdrew from Indochina.

w4_178.title: Sino-Indian Border Conflict
w4_178.detail: China and India clashed over the Himalayan border.

w4_179.title: Death of Mao Zedong
w4_179.detail: The leader of the Cultural Revolution died and China reached a turning point.

w4_180.title: Deng Xiaoping's Southern Tour
w4_180.detail: He called for accelerating reform and opening, moving toward a socialist market economy.

w4_181.title: China Joins the WTO
w4_181.detail: It joined the World Trade Organization, and trade expanded rapidly as the "world's factory."

w4_182.title: Beijing Olympics
w4_182.detail: The first Summer Olympics held in China.

w4_184.title: Founding of the New Kingdom
w4_184.detail: With Thebes as capital, Egypt expanded into western Asia and reached its peak.

w4_185.title: Queen Hatshepsut
w4_185.detail: She took the throne as a female pharaoh and sent trading expeditions.

w4_186.title: Akhenaten's Religious Reform
w4_186.detail: He had only the sun god Aten worshipped and moved the capital to Amarna.

w4_187.title: Tutankhamun
w4_187.detail: A boy king took the throne. His tomb, discovered in 1922, was found almost untouched.

w4_188.title: Founding of Carthage
w4_188.detail: A colony the Phoenicians built in North Africa, it prospered on Mediterranean maritime trade.

w4_190.title: Ptolemaic Dynasty
w4_190.detail: A dynasty founded by Alexander's general. It became the center of Hellenistic culture.

w4_191.title: Rosetta Stone
w4_191.detail: A stele carved with the same text in three scripts. Its discovery in 1799 led to the decipherment of hieroglyphs.

w4_192.title: Cleopatra VII
w4_192.detail: She allied with Caesar and Antony and tried to preserve Egypt's independence.

w4_193.title: Bantu Expansion
w4_193.detail: Carrying farming and ironworking, they moved south from West Africa. It changed the African continent's linguistic map.

w4_194.title: Vandal Kingdom
w4_194.detail: The Vandals crossed to North Africa and built a kingdom with Carthage as capital.

w4_195.title: Founding of Kairouan
w4_195.detail: An Islamic base city in North Africa built by Arab forces.

w4_196.title: Fatimid Caliphate
w4_196.detail: A Shia dynasty was founded in North Africa and later made Cairo its capital.

w4_197.title: Founding of Cairo
w4_197.detail: The new capital built by the Fatimids. It later became a center of learning and commerce in the Islamic world.

w4_198.title: Al-Azhar
w4_198.detail: The mosque and school built in Cairo is regarded as one of the world's oldest universities.

w4_199.title: Almoravid Dynasty
w4_199.detail: Berbers of the western Sahara founded it, ruling from Morocco to southern Spain.

w4_200.title: Ayyubid Dynasty
w4_200.detail: A dynasty Saladin founded in Egypt. It later fought the Crusaders.

w4_201.title: Mamluk Sultanate
w4_201.detail: A dynasty founded by soldiers of slave origin (mamluks). It halted the Mongol army in Egypt.

w4_202.title: Ibn Battuta's Travels
w4_202.detail: A Moroccan-born traveler spent about 30 years journeying through the Islamic world.

w4_203.title: Portuguese Capture of Ceuta
w4_203.detail: Portugal took Ceuta in Morocco, its first base for expansion into Africa.

w4_204.title: Portuguese Slave Trade from Africa
w4_204.detail: People seized on the West African coast were taken to Europe.

w4_205.title: Elmina Castle
w4_205.detail: A base Portugal built on the Gulf of Guinea. It became the center of the gold and slave trade.

w4_206.title: Ottoman Conquest of Egypt
w4_206.detail: It destroyed the Mamluk Sultanate and became protector of Mecca and Medina.

w4_207.title: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
w4_207.detail: The Portuguese king was killed in battle and Morocco kept its independence.

w4_208.title: Muhammad Ali
w4_208.detail: As governor of the Ottoman Empire he pursued modernization and became Egypt's actual ruler.

w4_209.title: Shaka of the Zulu Kingdom
w4_209.detail: He reformed the military system and built a powerful kingdom in southern Africa.

w4_210.title: French Capture of Algiers
w4_210.detail: France began the colonization of North Africa.

w4_211.title: Independence of Liberia
w4_211.detail: A country founded by freed Black slaves from America.

w4_212.title: Anglo-Zulu War
w4_212.detail: British forces fought the Zulu Kingdom, lost at Isandlwana, but later conquered it.

w4_213.title: British Occupation of Egypt
w4_213.detail: Britain occupied Egypt militarily to protect its interests in the Suez Canal.

w4_214.title: Fashoda Incident
w4_214.detail: British and French policies of crossing Africa north–south and east–west collided. An entente was later reached.

w4_215.title: Union of South Africa
w4_215.detail: Founded as a British dominion. White-centered politics continued.

w4_216.title: Italian Invasion of Ethiopia
w4_216.detail: Mussolini invaded Ethiopia and the League of Nations could not respond effectively.

w4_217.title: Egyptian Revolution
w4_217.detail: The Free Officers of Naguib, Nasser and others overthrew the monarchy.

w4_218.title: Algerian War
w4_218.detail: The National Liberation Front (FLN) began a war of independence and achieved independence in 1962.

w4_219.title: Independence of Ghana
w4_219.detail: It became the first independent country in sub-Saharan Africa.

w4_220.title: Organization of African Unity
w4_220.detail: An organization aiming at African solidarity and the end of colonialism. It later developed into the AU.

w4_221.title: Biafran War
w4_221.detail: Biafra in eastern Nigeria declared secession and civil war followed.

w4_222.title: Ethiopian Revolution
w4_222.detail: The military deposed Emperor Haile Selassie.

w4_223.title: Soweto Uprising
w4_223.detail: Police put down by force Black students protesting apartheid-era education.

w4_224.title: Independence of Zimbabwe
w4_224.detail: White rule ended and majority rule was realized.

w4_225.title: Release of Mandela and Namibian Independence
w4_225.detail: Released after 27 years in prison. The way to abolishing apartheid opened.

w4_226.title: Somali Civil War
w4_226.detail: The government collapsed, the country split and civil war followed.

w4_227.title: FIFA World Cup in South Africa
w4_227.detail: The first World Cup held on the African continent.

w4_228.title: African Continental Free Trade Area
w4_228.detail: African countries signed an agreement aiming to remove tariffs within the region.

w4_230.title: Caral Civilization
w4_230.detail: One of South America's oldest urban civilizations, built near Peru's coast.

w4_231.title: Chavín Culture
w4_231.detail: A religious culture that spread across the Andes. Stone carvings of jaguars and others remain.

w4_232.title: Nazca Lines
w4_232.detail: Giant birds and monkeys were drawn on Peru's desert. Their purpose remains a mystery.

w4_233.title: Teotihuacan
w4_233.detail: A huge city on the Mexican plateau. The "Pyramid of the Sun" and "Pyramid of the Moon" were built.

w4_234.title: Collapse of the Classic Maya
w4_234.detail: Cities in the southern lowlands were abandoned one after another. Drought and war are said to be the causes.

w4_235.title: Viking Vinland
w4_235.detail: Records tell of Leif Erikson and others reaching the North American continent, about 500 years before Columbus.

w4_236.title: Pueblo Culture
w4_236.detail: Native peoples of the American Southwest built stone settlements in cliffs.

w4_237.title: Aztec Triple Alliance
w4_237.detail: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan formed an alliance and ruled central Mexico.

w4_238.title: Cortés Lands in Mexico
w4_238.detail: A small Spanish force won native allies and marched on the Aztecs.

w4_239.title: Pizarro's Advance into the Inca Empire
w4_239.detail: At Cajamarca he captured Emperor Atahualpa, leading the Inca Empire to collapse.

w4_240.title: New Laws and Las Casas
w4_240.detail: The cleric Las Casas denounced the abuse of native peoples. The Spanish king banned enslaving them, but it was not obeyed.

w4_241.title: St. Augustine
w4_241.detail: Built by Spain in present-day Florida, the oldest European settlement in the United States.

w4_242.title: Founding of Quebec
w4_242.detail: A base of the French colony built by Champlain. It later became the center of French-speaking Canada.

w4_243.title: New Amsterdam
w4_243.detail: A colony built by the Dutch. It later came under British rule and was renamed New York.

w4_244.title: Harvard University
w4_244.detail: The oldest university in the United States, founded by Puritans.

w4_245.title: Salem Witch Trials
w4_245.detail: In Massachusetts, people suspected of witchcraft were tried and 20 were executed.

w4_246.title: French and Indian War
w4_246.detail: Britain and France fought for supremacy in North America, and Britain won and gained Canada and more.

w4_247.title: Stamp Act
w4_247.detail: Britain taxed the colonies and met the objection "no taxation without representation."

w4_248.title: Boston Tea Party
w4_248.detail: Colonists threw a ship's cargo of tea into the sea. It opened the way to the War of Independence.

w4_249.title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
w4_249.detail: The first battles of the American War of Independence.

w4_250.title: Battle of Yorktown
w4_250.detail: A Franco-American force made the British surrender, and the outcome of the war of independence was nearly settled.

w4_252.title: US Constitution
w4_252.detail: One of the world's oldest written constitutions, establishing separation of powers and federalism.

w4_253.title: Bill of Rights
w4_253.detail: Ten amendments added to the US Constitution, guaranteeing freedoms such as speech and religion.

w4_254.title: Lewis and Clark Expedition
w4_254.detail: An expedition that reached the Pacific overland from the Mississippi.

w4_255.title: War of 1812
w4_255.detail: America declared war on Britain, and even the White House was burned.

w4_256.title: Mexican Independence
w4_256.detail: After about eleven years of war of independence, Mexico became independent from Spain.

w4_257.title: Indian Removal Act
w4_257.detail: Native peoples were forcibly relocated to reservations in the West. The "Trail of Tears" is its tragedy.

w4_258.title: Battle of the Alamo
w4_258.detail: Over Texas independence, a small garrison was besieged by the Mexican army and wiped out.

w4_259.title: Mexican–American War
w4_259.detail: America gained vast territory from Mexico, including California.

w4_260.title: Seneca Falls Convention
w4_260.detail: The first convention calling for women's rights, which issued the "Declaration of Sentiments."

w4_261.title: John Brown's Raid
w4_261.detail: He rose in armed revolt demanding abolition of slavery, but failed and was executed.

w4_262.title: Assassination of Lincoln
w4_262.detail: Just after the Civil War ended, he was shot while watching a play and died.

w4_263.title: Alaska Purchase
w4_263.detail: America bought Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million.

w4_264.title: Statue of Liberty
w4_264.detail: A statue given by France was erected in New York harbor.

w4_265.title: Wounded Knee Massacre
w4_265.detail: US troops killed Sioux people. Fighting with native peoples effectively ended.

w4_266.title: Assassination of McKinley
w4_266.detail: Theodore Roosevelt became president at age 42.

w4_267.title: Mexican Revolution
w4_267.detail: A revolution against Díaz's dictatorship began and became a ten-year civil war.

w4_268.title: Federal Reserve System
w4_268.detail: America's central banking system was launched.

w4_269.title: US Enters World War I
w4_269.detail: It entered the war citing German unrestricted submarine warfare and other reasons.

w4_270.title: Women's Suffrage and Prohibition
w4_270.detail: Women gained the vote by the 19th Amendment. Prohibition was also enforced.

w4_271.title: Lindbergh's Atlantic Crossing
w4_271.detail: He flew solo nonstop from New York to Paris and became an international hero.

w4_272.title: Bretton Woods Agreement
w4_272.detail: It set the postwar international monetary system and created the IMF and World Bank.

w4_273.title: Brown v. Board of Education
w4_273.detail: Racial segregation in public schools was ruled unconstitutional.

w4_274.title: Montgomery Bus Boycott
w4_274.detail: Triggered by Rosa Parks' arrest, Black citizens refused to use the buses for about a year.

w4_275.title: March on Washington
w4_275.detail: Martin Luther King Jr. gave his "I Have a Dream" speech. President Kennedy was assassinated that same year.

w4_276.title: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
w4_276.detail: The civil rights leader was assassinated. Riots broke out in many places.

w4_277.title: Watergate Scandal
w4_277.detail: President Nixon was forced to resign.

w4_278.title: IBM PC
w4_278.detail: IBM released a personal computer, and PCs began to spread to businesses and homes.

w4_279.title: NAFTA Takes Effect
w4_279.detail: The free-trade agreement of the US, Canada and Mexico took effect.

w4_280.title: iPhone Release
w4_280.detail: It became the occasion for smartphones to spread worldwide.

w4_281.title: Obama Inaugurated
w4_281.detail: He became the first African American president of the United States.

w4_282.title: Cultivation of Maize
w4_282.detail: In Mexico, maize was developed from the wild plant teosinte. A crop that supported agriculture in the Americas.

w4_283.title: San Lorenzo and La Venta
w4_283.detail: Centers of the Olmec. Colossal stone heads remain.

w4_284.title: Monte Albán
w4_284.detail: A mountaintop city of the Zapotec civilization in southern Mexico.

w4_285.title: Maya Script
w4_285.detail: The oldest example was found at the Guatemalan site San Bartolo.

w4_286.title: Moche Culture
w4_286.detail: On Peru's northern coast it flourished with irrigated agriculture and fine pottery and gold work.

w4_287.title: Tikal and Teotihuacan
w4_287.detail: The Maya city Tikal is thought to have been influenced by Teotihuacan's power.

w4_288.title: Tiwanaku and Wari
w4_288.detail: In the Andes, Tiwanaku (Bolivia) and Wari (Peru) each flourished as great powers.

w4_289.title: Death of King Pakal
w4_289.detail: King of the Maya city Palenque. His great tomb temple has been excavated.

w4_290.title: Decline of Teotihuacan
w4_290.detail: The huge city on the Mexican plateau declined through fire and abandonment.

w4_291.title: Toltec Civilization
w4_291.detail: A warrior culture flourished centered on Tula in central Mexico.

w4_292.title: Chichén Itzá
w4_292.detail: A Maya city on the Yucatán Peninsula. The stepped pyramid "El Castillo" stands there.

w4_293.title: Cahokia's Prosperity
w4_293.detail: A city of great earthen mounds in the Mississippi basin. At its peak, tens of thousands may have lived there.

w4_294.title: Chimú Kingdom
w4_294.detail: A kingdom that spread along Peru's northern coast. It was later annexed by the Inca Empire.

w4_295.title: Inca Origin Legend
w4_295.detail: The tale of Manco Cápac, founder of Cusco, is told.

w4_296.title: Radio Drama "The War of the Worlds"
w4_296.detail: Orson Welles' broadcast was taken by some listeners as a real event.

w4_297.title: Scopes Trial
w4_297.detail: A trial over whether evolution may be taught in schools.

w4_298.title: Social Security Act
w4_298.detail: It set up unemployment insurance and pensions. A pillar of New Deal policy.

w4_299.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
w4_299.detail: Japanese forces attacked the US naval base in Hawaii and the US entered World War II.

w4_300.title: San Francisco Conference
w4_300.detail: Fifty countries met and adopted the UN Charter.

w4_301.title: Ötzi the Iceman
w4_301.detail: A 5,000-year-old mummy found in the Alps. He carried a copper axe and a bow and arrows.

w4_302.title: Newgrange
w4_302.detail: A huge tomb in Ireland. The winter-solstice sunrise shines deep inside.

w4_303.title: Stonehenge
w4_303.detail: A huge stone circle in England. A connection with calendars and ritual is thought likely.

w4_304.title: Minoan Civilization
w4_304.detail: Centered on the Palace of Knossos on Crete, it flourished on maritime trade.

w4_305.title: Mycenaean Civilization
w4_305.detail: On mainland Greece, a civilization with citadels and rich golden tombs arose.

w4_306.title: Uluburun Shipwreck
w4_306.detail: A Bronze Age ship found off Turkey. It tells of wide Mediterranean trade.

w4_307.title: Dorian Migration South
w4_307.detail: The Dorians invaded Greece and the Mycenaean civilization collapsed.

w4_308.title: The Etruscans
w4_308.detail: They built city-states in central Italy and later passed their culture to Rome.

w4_309.title: Hallstatt Culture
w4_309.detail: An early iron culture centered on salt mines in Austria. It leads to the later Celtic culture.

w4_310.title: Sun Chariot
w4_310.detail: A bronze figure of a horse-drawn chariot pulling the sun, found in Denmark. It conveys the prayers of Nordic Bronze Age people.

w4_311.title: East African Campaign
w4_311.detail: In Africa too, fighting took place over Germany's colonies in World War I.

w4_312.title: Egyptian Revolution of 1919
w4_312.detail: Resentment of British protectorate rule rose and an independence movement began.

w4_313.title: Discovery of Tutankhamun's Tomb
w4_313.detail: Howard Carter found an almost untouched tomb in the Valley of the Kings.

w4_314.title: Accession of Haile Selassie
w4_314.detail: He took the throne as Ethiopian emperor. He later led the founding of the Organization of African Unity.

w4_315.title: Liberation of Ethiopia
w4_315.detail: With British support, Ethiopia was freed from Italian rule.

w4_316.title: Battle of El Alamein
w4_316.detail: In North Africa the Allies defeated the Axis, a turning point of the war.

w4_317.title: Operation Torch
w4_317.detail: Allied forces landed in North Africa and caught the Axis in a pincer.

socrates.name: Socrates
socrates.detail: Questioned people on street corners until they recognized their own ignorance. Later sentenced to death at trial.
socrates.lesson: "I know that I know nothing" — learning begins with doubt.

alexander.name: Alexander the Great
alexander.detail: Set out east in his twenties and conquered lands from Egypt to northwestern India.

aristotle.name: Aristotle
aristotle.detail: "Father of all learning": logic, natural science, politics and more. Also tutor to Alexander.

caesar.name: Julius Caesar
caesar.detail: Conquered Gaul and became dictator, but was assassinated by defenders of the Republic.

augustus.name: Augustus
augustus.detail: Kept the outward form of the Republic while building a de facto empire, bringing the Pax Romana.

constantine.name: Constantine
constantine.detail: Legalized Christianity and moved the capital to Constantinople.

charlemagne.name: Charlemagne
charlemagne.detail: Unified most of western Europe and was crowned Roman emperor by the pope.

leonardo.name: Leonardo da Vinci
leonardo.detail: Crossed painting, anatomy and mechanical design, valuing observation and experiment.
leonardo.lesson: Observing across disciplines produces new discoveries.

gutenberg.name: Gutenberg
gutenberg.detail: Combined movable type with the printing press to mass-produce the Bible.

columbus.name: Columbus
columbus.detail: Sailed west hoping to reach Asia and arrived in the Caribbean. His voyage also opened the way to conquest and exploitation.

luther.name: Martin Luther
luther.detail: Criticized the Church in his Ninety-five Theses and sparked the Reformation.

galileo.name: Galileo
galileo.detail: Observed the heavens with a telescope, supported heliocentrism, and was tried by the Church.

newton.name: Newton
newton.detail: Set out universal gravitation and the laws of motion, framing modern science.

louis14.name: Louis XIV
louis14.detail: Reigned over seventy years and became the symbol of absolute monarchy. Built the Palace of Versailles.

rousseau.name: Rousseau
rousseau.detail: Argued for popular sovereignty in The Social Contract, influencing the French Revolution.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.detail: Ended the post-revolutionary chaos, became emperor, and spread war and law across Europe.

darwin.name: Darwin
darwin.detail: In On the Origin of Species, argued that living things evolve by natural selection.

marx.name: Marx
marx.detail: Analyzed capitalism in Das Kapital and influenced later socialist movements.

victoria.name: Queen Victoria
victoria.detail: Reigned for over sixty-three years, symbolizing the British Empire at its height.

bismarck.name: Bismarck
bismarck.detail: Led German unification through "blood and iron" and kept Europe balanced with a web of alliances.

lenin.name: Lenin
lenin.detail: Led the Russian Revolution and became the first leader of the Soviet Union.

einstein.name: Einstein
einstein.detail: Published the theory of relativity. Later emigrated to the US and warned of the dangers of nuclear weapons.

hitler.name: Hitler
hitler.detail: Took power legally and brought about wars of aggression and the Holocaust.
hitler.lesson: Even democratic procedures can be exploited by dictators when conditions allow.

churchill.name: Churchill
churchill.detail: Led Britain in World War II and, after the war, described the start of the Cold War as an "iron curtain."

gorbachev.name: Gorbachev
gorbachev.role: Last leader of the Soviet Union
gorbachev.detail: Pursued perestroika and the end of the Cold War, but the USSR collapsed.

jeanne.name: Joan of Arc
jeanne.detail: Inspired French forces in the Hundred Years' War but was executed as a heretic. Later made a saint.

elizabeth1.name: Elizabeth I
elizabeth1.detail: Defeated the Spanish Armada and laid the foundation for England's rise as a maritime power.

buddha.name: Buddha
buddha.detail: Gave up his princely status and taught liberation from suffering. (Dates are uncertain.)

confucius.name: Confucius
confucius.detail: Taught government by virtue and ritual; his disciples' words were compiled as the Analects.

shihuangdi.name: Qin Shi Huang
shihuangdi.detail: First unifier of China; standardized writing, weights and measures, and currency. Also known for the Great Wall and the Terracotta Army.

zhangqian.name: Zhang Qian
zhangqian.detail: Traveled to the Western Regions on Emperor Wu's orders and opened what became the Silk Road.

xuanzang.name: Xuanzang
xuanzang.detail: Spent over a decade traveling to India and brought back and translated a vast body of Buddhist texts. Model for Journey to the West.

taizong.name: Taizong (Li Shimin)
taizong.detail: Employed talented officials and ruled stably, an era called the "Reign of Zhenguan."

harun.name: Harun al-Rashid
harun.detail: Caliph at the peak of the dynasty, when learning and culture flourished around Baghdad.

avicenna.name: Avicenna (Ibn Sina)
avicenna.detail: His Canon of Medicine became a textbook in European universities for centuries.

genghis.name: Genghis Khan
genghis.detail: United the nomadic tribes and laid the foundation of an empire spanning Eurasia.

kublai.name: Kublai Khan
kublai.detail: Set his capital at Dadu and founded the Yuan dynasty. Also sent expeditions against Japan.

zhenghe.name: Zheng He
zhenghe.detail: Rose from eunuch to admiral and led great fleets into the Indian Ocean seven times.

akbar.name: Akbar
akbar.detail: Adopted religiously tolerant policies and consolidated the Mughal Empire.

kangxi.name: Kangxi Emperor
kangxi.detail: Reigned sixty-one years and laid the foundation for the Qing's golden age.

gandhi.name: Gandhi
gandhi.role: Leader of the Indian independence movement
gandhi.detail: Led a movement of nonviolence and civil disobedience and guided India to independence. Was assassinated.

sunyat.name: Sun Yat-sen
sunyat.detail: Led the Xinhai Revolution and became the first provisional president of the Republic of China.

mao.name: Mao Zedong
mao.role: Founder of the People's Republic of China
mao.detail: Proclaimed the founding of the PRC. The Great Leap Forward and Cultural Revolution also caused great turmoil.

ho.name: Ho Chi Minh
ho.detail: Led Vietnam's independence movement and became the first president of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

deng.name: Deng Xiaoping
deng.detail: Pushed reform and opening-up, driving China into rapid growth.

ramses.name: Ramesses II
ramses.detail: Reigned over sixty years and left great monuments such as Abu Simbel.

cleopatra.name: Cleopatra VII
cleopatra.detail: Last queen of the Ptolemaic dynasty. Allied with Roman leaders to try to preserve Egypt's independence.

hannibal.name: Hannibal
hannibal.detail: Crossed the Alps with elephants and threatened Rome itself.

augustine.name: Augustine
augustine.detail: North African Church Father. Wrote Confessions and shaped Western Christian thought.

musa.name: Mansa Musa
musa.detail: Made the pilgrimage to Mecca carrying vast amounts of gold, making his wealth known across the Mediterranean world.

battuta.name: Ibn Battuta
battuta.detail: Set out from Morocco, traveled across Africa and Asia, and left the Rihla (Travels).

muhammad_ali.name: Muhammad Ali
muhammad_ali.detail: Modernized the army, industry and education, laying the foundation of modern Egypt.

menelik.name: Menelik II
menelik.detail: Defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa and preserved Ethiopian independence.

nkrumah.name: Nkrumah
nkrumah.detail: Led the first sub-Saharan independence and championed African unity.

nasser.name: Nasser
nasser.detail: Nationalized the Suez Canal and became a symbol of Arab nationalism.

lumumba.name: Lumumba
lumumba.role: First prime minister of the Congo
lumumba.detail: Ousted amid the chaos just after independence, and killed.

mandela.name: Mandela
mandela.detail: After twenty-seven years in prison, became the country's first Black president.
mandela.lesson: He sought unity through reconciliation, not revenge.

maathai.name: Wangari Maathai
maathai.detail: Led the tree-planting Green Belt Movement and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

moctezuma.name: Moctezuma II
moctezuma.detail: King when the Spanish arrived. Died amid the turmoil.

atahualpa.name: Atahualpa
atahualpa.detail: Captured by Pizarro; he paid a ransom but was executed.

cortes.name: Cortés
cortes.detail: Conquered the Aztec Empire using indigenous allies and disease.

washington.name: Washington
washington.detail: Commanded the army in the War of Independence and later became the first president.

jefferson.name: Jefferson
jefferson.detail: Drafted the Declaration of Independence. Yet he owned slaves.

franklin.name: Franklin
franklin.detail: Known for his lightning experiment and publishing; also helped draft the Declaration of Independence.

toussaint.name: Toussaint Louverture
toussaint.detail: Rose from slavery to lead the liberation army and the Haitian Revolution.

bolivar.name: Bolívar
bolivar.detail: Led the independence of Venezuela, Colombia and more, and was called "the Liberator."

lincoln.name: Lincoln
lincoln.detail: Saw the nation through the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation. Was assassinated.

edison.name: Edison
edison.detail: Changed industry with many inventions, including the incandescent bulb and phonograph.

fdr.name: F. D. Roosevelt
fdr.detail: Carried out the New Deal and led the Allies in World War II.

oppenheimer.name: Oppenheimer
oppenheimer.detail: Led the Manhattan Project and later warned of nuclear dangers.

kennedy.name: Kennedy
kennedy.detail: Handled the Cuban Missile Crisis and set a Moon landing as a national goal. Was assassinated.

king.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
king.detail: Led the nonviolent civil rights movement and gave the "I Have a Dream" speech. Was assassinated.

armstrong.name: Armstrong
armstrong.detail: On Apollo 11, became the first human to walk on the Moon.

jobs.name: Steve Jobs
jobs.detail: Changed the shape of information devices with the personal computer and the iPhone.

shotoku.name: Prince Shotoku
shotoku.detail: Established the twelve cap ranks and the Seventeen-Article Constitution, and sent envoys to Sui China.

nobunaga.name: Oda Nobunaga
nobunaga.detail: Made use of firearms and moved the economy with free markets (rakuichi-rakuza). Fell at Honnō-ji.

meiji.name: Emperor Meiji
meiji.detail: Symbol of building a modern state, from the Charter Oath to the promulgation of the constitution.

darius1.name: Darius I
darius1.detail: Divided the empire into provinces and built a road network and coinage, bringing it to its peak. Also known for his defeat at Marathon.
darius1.lesson: A vast state is held together by roads and institutions.

pericles.name: Pericles
pericles.detail: Led democracy at its height and promoted the rebuilding of the Parthenon. Died of the plague.
pericles.lesson: Citizen participation produced the city's power and culture.

herodotus.name: Herodotus
herodotus.detail: Recorded the customs of many peoples, centered on the Persian Wars; called the "Father of History."
herodotus.lesson: The practice of "inquiring" into and telling the past began.

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras
pythagoras.detail: Held that all things are number and studied the ratios of pitch to string length. Known for the Pythagorean theorem (though whether he discovered it is debated).
pythagoras.lesson: He saw an order of numbers behind nature.

plato.name: Plato
plato.detail: Disciple of Socrates who founded the Academy. Wrote on the theory of Forms and the Republic, laying the foundation of Western philosophy.
plato.lesson: He grew his teacher's questions into a system.

hippocrates.name: Hippocrates
hippocrates.detail: Valued medicine that sought natural causes of disease rather than divine punishment. Regarded as a source of medical ethics.
hippocrates.lesson: The starting point of medicine based on experience and observation.

archimedes.name: Archimedes
archimedes.detail: Studied buoyancy and the lever, and calculated pi precisely. Died during the siege of Syracuse.

mencius.name: Mencius
mencius.detail: Taught that human nature is good and called for government that cherishes the people.
mencius.lesson: He advocated politics that trusts in human goodness.

liubang.name: Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu of Han)
liubang.detail: Of peasant origin, he used talent well to defeat Xiang Yu and founded the Han.
liubang.lesson: He could employ people better than himself.

xiangyu.name: Xiang Yu
xiangyu.detail: Destroyed the Qin with overwhelming martial prowess, but lost to Liu Bang and killed himself at Gaixia.
xiangyu.lesson: Strength alone could not win the realm.

wudi.name: Emperor Wu
wudi.detail: Fought the Xiongnu, sent Zhang Qian to open contact with the Western Regions, and made Confucianism the state teaching.
wudi.lesson: He pursued expansion and institutionalization at once.

simaqian.name: Sima Qian
simaqian.detail: Endured the humiliation of castration and completed the Records of the Grand Historian, creating the biographical style centered on people.
simaqian.lesson: He kept writing through hardship for later generations.

ashoka.name: Ashoka
ashoka.detail: Regretting the horrors of war, he embraced Buddhism and had laws carved on pillars, aiming at rule by compassion.
ashoka.lesson: A victor's remorse changed the ideals of government.

scipio.name: Scipio
scipio.detail: Defeated Hannibal at Zama and earned the title "Africanus."
scipio.lesson: The one who studied the enemy best defeated the enemy.

cicero.name: Cicero
cicero.detail: Defended the Republic with eloquence but was killed in the turmoil after Caesar's death.
cicero.lesson: The power of words is tested before power.

nero.name: Nero
nero.detail: Rebuilt the city after the Great Fire of Rome, but persecuted Christians and killed himself amid revolt.
nero.lesson: He loved the arts but misgoverned.

hadrian.name: Hadrian
hadrian.detail: Prioritized defense over expansion and built a wall in Britain. Loved Greek culture.
hadrian.lesson: Governing by fixing borders, not just expanding.

aurelius.name: Marcus Aurelius
aurelius.detail: Last of the Five Good Emperors. A Stoic philosopher who left the Meditations.
aurelius.lesson: Even in the field camp, he reflected on himself.

caocao.name: Cao Cao
caocao.role: Warlord who laid the foundation of Wei
caocao.detail: Defeated rival warlords, unified northern China, and was also a renowned poet.
caocao.lesson: A powerful figure of turbulent times, he excelled in verse as well.

liubei.name: Liu Bei
liubei.detail: Swore brotherhood with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, welcomed Zhuge Liang, and founded Shu.
liubei.lesson: The virtue that gathers people turned a small force into a state.

zhugeliang.name: Zhuge Liang
zhugeliang.detail: Recruited by Liu Bei through the "Three Visits," he supported Shu as strategist and statesman. Died in camp during the Northern Expeditions.
zhugeliang.lesson: Talent and sincerity sustained a small state.

justinian.name: Justinian I
justinian.detail: Compiled the Corpus Juris Civilis and rebuilt the Hagia Sophia. Also tried to recover the old western Mediterranean territories.
justinian.lesson: He reorganized the Roman tradition through law and architecture.

wuzetian.name: Wu Zetian
wuzetian.detail: The only woman to rule China as emperor. Built up the bureaucracy by employing men who passed the civil service exams.
wuzetian.lesson: She employed able people regardless of background.

xuanzong.name: Xuanzong
xuanzong.detail: Brought the Tang to its peak in the Kaiyuan era, but late in life doted on Yang Guifei and invited the An Lushan Rebellion.
xuanzong.lesson: Complacency after the peak invited rebellion.

libai.name: Li Bai
libai.detail: Called the "Poet Immortal," known for free-spirited verse on wine and the moon.
libai.lesson: The power of words unbound by form.

dufu.name: Du Fu
dufu.detail: Called the "Poet Sage," he wrote of the people's suffering amid the An Lushan Rebellion.
dufu.lesson: Recording turbulent times was also poetry's task.

saladin.name: Saladin
saladin.detail: Retook Jerusalem yet was also generous to captured enemies. He and Richard I held each other in mutual respect.
saladin.lesson: A leader who showed courtesy even to enemies.

richard1.name: Richard I
richard1.detail: Led the Third Crusade and was called "the Lionheart." Spent most of his reign abroad.
richard1.lesson: A valiant king fought far from his kingdom.

william1.name: William I
william1.detail: As Duke of Normandy, conquered England and ordered the Domesday Book land survey.
william1.lesson: After conquest comes surveying in order to rule.

frederick2.name: Frederick II
frederick2.detail: Valued learning and coexistence of religions in Sicily, and regained Jerusalem through diplomacy. Called "Stupor Mundi."
frederick2.lesson: An emperor open to other cultures.

aquinas.name: Thomas Aquinas
aquinas.detail: Synthesized Aristotelian philosophy and Christian theology in the Summa Theologiae.

dante.name: Dante
dante.detail: Wrote the Divine Comedy in Tuscan rather than Latin, building literature in the vernacular.
dante.lesson: Writing in one's own language broadened literature.

zhuyuanzhang.name: Zhu Yuanzhang (Hongwu Emperor)
zhuyuanzhang.detail: Rose from poor peasant to monk, to the Red Turbans, to emperor. Strengthened imperial power and thoroughly centralized rule.
zhuyuanzhang.lesson: Rising from the lowest rank, he gathered all power in his hands.

timur.name: Timur
timur.detail: Built a vast empire from Central to West Asia, with Samarkand as capital. Died of illness on a campaign against the Ming.
timur.lesson: A conqueror who adorned his capital with magnificent architecture.

yongle.name: Yongle Emperor
yongle.detail: Moved the capital to Beijing and compiled the Yongle Encyclopedia. Also ordered Zheng He's great voyages.
yongle.lesson: He pursued expansion and compilation at once.

lorenzo.name: Lorenzo de' Medici
lorenzo.detail: Built wealth as a banker and patronized artists such as Botticelli and Michelangelo.
lorenzo.lesson: How wealth is spent nurtured the Renaissance.

michelangelo.name: Michelangelo
michelangelo.detail: Known for the David and the Sistine Chapel ceiling; also involved in designing St. Peter's Basilica.

raphael.name: Raphael
raphael.detail: Known for harmonious Madonnas and The School of Athens. Died at 37.
raphael.lesson: He painted ideal beauty while still young.

machiavelli.name: Machiavelli
machiavelli.detail: In The Prince, separated morality from politics and analyzed real power.
machiavelli.lesson: A political science that faced reality over ideals.

copernicus.name: Copernicus
copernicus.detail: Proposed heliocentrism in On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres, said to have been published just before his death.
copernicus.lesson: He took Earth down from the center of the universe.

magellan.name: Magellan
magellan.detail: Led a Spanish fleet on a circumnavigation but was killed in the Philippines.
magellan.lesson: The leader never saw the result.

calvin.name: Calvin
calvin.detail: Pursued theocratic reform in Geneva and taught predestination. Taught that one's occupation is a calling from God.
calvin.lesson: An ethic of diligence and asceticism spread among merchants and craftsmen.

suleiman.name: Suleiman I
suleiman.detail: Called "the Magnificent" and "the Lawgiver," he besieged Vienna and organized a legal system.
suleiman.lesson: He led the empire to its golden age through military and law.

shakespeare.name: Shakespeare
shakespeare.detail: Wrote Hamlet, Macbeth and more. His portrayals of human complexity are still staged worldwide.
shakespeare.lesson: He put the movements of the human heart on stage in words.

kepler.name: Kepler
kepler.detail: Derived three laws of planetary motion, based on Tycho Brahe's observational data.
kepler.lesson: Precise observational data revealed the laws.

descartes.name: Descartes
descartes.detail: Said "I think, therefore I am," showing a method of reasoning from an undoubtable foundation. Also originated coordinates.
descartes.lesson: He rebuilt certain knowledge starting from doubt.

cromwell.name: Cromwell
cromwell.detail: Led the parliamentary army in the Puritan Revolution and ruled the republic as Lord Protector after the king's execution.
cromwell.lesson: A revolutionary leader became a de facto dictator.

peter1.name: Peter the Great
peter1.detail: Learned from the West himself, built a navy and a new capital, and led Russia toward a modern state.
peter1.lesson: An emperor who learned in person and remade the whole country.

catherine2.name: Catherine II
catherine2.detail: Showed interest in Enlightenment ideas while expanding territory, annexing Crimea and joining the partitions of Poland.
catherine2.lesson: An empress who combined enlightenment with autocracy.

frederick_g.name: Frederick the Great
frederick_g.detail: Said the monarch is "the first servant of the state," practiced enlightened absolutism, and expanded territory in conflict with Austria.
frederick_g.lesson: He made a small state strong with a modern army and bureaucracy.

maria_theresa.name: Maria Theresa
maria_theresa.detail: Endured the War of the Austrian Succession and advanced administrative and educational reform. Bore sixteen children; the youngest was Marie Antoinette.
maria_theresa.lesson: She ruled as a mother who defended and organized the state.

smith.name: Adam Smith
smith.detail: In The Wealth of Nations, explained the workings of the division of labor and free markets. Regarded as the father of modern economics.
smith.lesson: He saw individual self-interest as leading to social prosperity.

kant.name: Kant
kant.detail: In the Critique of Pure Reason, analyzed the framework by which people perceive the world. His daily walk was said to be so exact that neighbors set clocks by it.
kant.lesson: He tested the limits of reason by reason itself.

voltaire.name: Voltaire
voltaire.detail: Criticized religious intolerance and defended freedom of speech. Said to have declared "I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it" (a later paraphrase).
voltaire.lesson: A sardonic wit who preached tolerance.

watt.name: Watt
watt.detail: Greatly improved the steam engine and spread the power source of the Industrial Revolution. The unit "watt" is named for him.
watt.lesson: Small improvements became the power that moved an age.

robespierre.name: Robespierre
robespierre.detail: As Jacobin leader, carried out the Reign of Terror and was himself later executed.
robespierre.lesson: Politics pursuing purity of ideals tilted toward violence.

mozart.name: Mozart
mozart.detail: Composed over 600 works before dying at 35, including The Marriage of Figaro and The Magic Flute.
mozart.lesson: Natural gift and a prodigious work ethic.

beethoven.name: Beethoven
beethoven.detail: Wrote masterpieces such as the Ninth Symphony even after going nearly deaf. Opened the way for musicians to live as free artists.
beethoven.lesson: In hardship he made his greatest music.

wilberforce.name: Wilberforce
wilberforce.detail: Pleaded in Parliament for years for the abolition of the slave trade, achieved in 1807.
wilberforce.lesson: One person's persistent appeals moved the law.

nightingale.name: Nightingale
nightingale.detail: Reformed field hospitals in the Crimean War and used statistics to press for better sanitation. Founder of modern nursing.
nightingale.lesson: A reformer who persuaded with numbers.

garibaldi.name: Garibaldi
garibaldi.detail: Led the volunteer Red Shirts to take Sicily and southern Italy and handed them to the King of Sardinia.
garibaldi.lesson: He did not claim unification as his own achievement.

pasteur.name: Pasteur
pasteur.detail: Developed pasteurization and made vaccines such as rabies. Showed that germs cause disease.
pasteur.lesson: He fought an invisible enemy through experiment.

tolstoy.name: Tolstoy
tolstoy.detail: Wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina. In later years preached nonviolence, influencing Gandhi.

nietzsche.name: Nietzsche
nietzsche.detail: Declared "God is dead" and questioned existing values. Wrote Thus Spoke Zarathustra and more.
nietzsche.lesson: Sharp thought that doubts received values.

bell.name: Alexander Graham Bell
bell.detail: Invented the telephone and also worked on education for the deaf.
bell.lesson: He made a tool to carry the human voice far.

freud.name: Freud
freud.detail: Focused on the workings of the unconscious, analyzing the mind through dreams and slips of the tongue. Greatly influenced 20th-century thought and literature.
freud.lesson: He gave theory to the unseen movements of the mind.

curie.name: Marie Curie
curie.detail: Studied radioactivity and discovered polonium and radium. Won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry.
curie.lesson: A scientist who crossed the barrier of gender.

picasso.name: Picasso
picasso.detail: Co-founded Cubism and denounced the bombing in the Spanish Civil War in Guernica. Produced tens of thousands of works in his lifetime.
picasso.lesson: An art of breaking forms and remaking them.

kemal.name: Kemal Atatürk
kemal.role: First president of the Republic of Turkey
kemal.detail: After the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire, founded the republic and pursued secularism and script reform.
kemal.lesson: Radical reforms renewed the shape of the nation.

stalin.name: Stalin
stalin.detail: Industrialized through five-year plans, while the Great Purge killed millions. Defeated Germany in World War II.
stalin.lesson: Industrialization and purges, victory and terror coexisted.

mussolini.name: Mussolini
mussolini.detail: Built the world's first Fascist regime and moved on to invading Ethiopia and allying with Germany.
mussolini.lesson: He toppled democracy with oratory and violence.

truman.name: Truman
truman.detail: Decided to use the atomic bomb and set the course of the Cold War with the Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan.
truman.lesson: Heavy decisions pressed on him in rapid succession.

nehru.name: Nehru
nehru.detail: Independence movement leader who championed nonalignment. His daughter Indira Gandhi also became prime minister.
nehru.lesson: He sought a path belonging to neither great-power camp.

degaulle.name: de Gaulle
degaulle.detail: Called for resistance from London under Nazi occupation and founded the Fifth Republic after the war.
degaulle.lesson: An unyielding will protected the nation's pride.

chaplin.name: Chaplin
chaplin.detail: Satirized poverty and power through comedy in works such as The Great Dictator.
chaplin.lesson: Laughter was criticism that reached the farthest.

reagan.name: Reagan
reagan.detail: Pursued tax cuts and a military buildup, then advanced nuclear arms reduction in talks with Gorbachev.
reagan.lesson: He shifted from hard line to dialogue.

thatcher.name: Thatcher
thatcher.detail: Pursued privatization and deregulation and was called the "Iron Lady." Also led Britain in the Falklands War.
thatcher.lesson: She carried out strong, divisive reforms.

annan.name: Kofi Annan
annan.detail: First UN Secretary-General from sub-Saharan Africa. Won the 2001 Nobel Peace Prize (together with the UN).
annan.lesson: He put resolution through dialogue at the center of the UN.

shaka.name: Shaka Zulu
shaka.detail: Raised the Zulu to a major power in southern Africa through military reform and the short spear.
shaka.lesson: Innovation in military organization strengthened a state.

njinga.name: Nzinga
njinga.detail: Fought the Portuguese slave trade and defended her kingdom for decades through diplomacy and war.
njinga.lesson: A queen who kept independence through negotiation and combat.

askia.name: Askia Muhammad
askia.detail: Brought the empire to its height and made Timbuktu flourish as a center of learning.
askia.lesson: A ruler who combined trade and scholarship.

haile_selassie.name: Haile Selassie I
haile_selassie.detail: Appealed to the League of Nations against Italian invasion. Later helped found the Organization of African Unity.
haile_selassie.lesson: A small nation's appeal was put before the world.

kenyatta.name: Kenyatta
kenyatta.detail: Imprisoned on suspicion over the Mau Mau uprising, he became the first president after independence.
kenyatta.lesson: From detention to father of independence.

nyerere.name: Nyerere
nyerere.detail: Built a socialist nation under the banner of "Ujamaa" (familyhood) and was called "Mwalimu" (teacher) by the people.
nyerere.lesson: A founding father who prized education.

sankara.name: Sankara
sankara.detail: Fought corruption and advanced women's status and self-sufficiency. Assassinated at 37.
sankara.lesson: Even a short term left vivid reforms.

sitting_bull.name: Sitting Bull
sitting_bull.detail: Resisted white settlement and defeated the cavalry at the Battle of the Little Bighorn. Later killed.
sitting_bull.lesson: He fought to defend the land to the end.

douglass.name: Frederick Douglass
douglass.detail: Escaped slavery to freedom and called for abolition through speeches and writings.
douglass.lesson: The voice of those directly affected became the movement's strength.

tubman.name: Harriet Tubman
tubman.detail: After escaping herself, led dozens of enslaved people to freedom on the Underground Railroad. Also served as a scout in the Civil War.
tubman.lesson: She used her own freedom for others.

troosevelt.name: Theodore Roosevelt
troosevelt.detail: Expanded influence abroad through "big stick" diplomacy and also worked to protect national parks.
troosevelt.lesson: He had two faces: conservation and imperialism.

ford.name: Henry Ford
ford.detail: Mass-produced the Model T on the assembly line and raised workers' wages.
ford.lesson: Mass production prepared the consumer society.

wilson.name: Wilson
wilson.detail: After World War I, proposed national self-determination and the League of Nations, but his own Congress refused to join.
wilson.lesson: His ideal was stopped by his own legislature.

kahlo.name: Frida Kahlo
kahlo.detail: Painted her own pain, body and Mexican culture in vivid self-portraits.
kahlo.lesson: She turned personal pain into expression that outlasts its time.

guevara.name: Che Guevara
guevara.detail: Took part in the Cuban Revolution and was killed in Bolivia. His portrait is used as a symbol worldwide.
guevara.lesson: A life lived for ideals became a symbol.

parks.name: Rosa Parks
parks.detail: Arrested for refusing to give up her bus seat to a white passenger, sparking the Montgomery Bus Boycott.
parks.lesson: A single refusal ignited a movement.

malcolmx.name: Malcolm X
malcolmx.detail: Called for Black self-respect and self-defense. After the pilgrimage to Mecca he also turned toward racial harmony, but was assassinated.
malcolmx.lesson: An activist with the courage to change his mind.

tipu.name: Tipu Sultan
tipu.detail: Called the "Tiger of Mysore," he fought the British East India Company using rocket weapons.
tipu.lesson: Even the latest weapons could not beat the gap in allies behind them.

qianlong.name: Qianlong Emperor
qianlong.detail: Brought the Qing to its height and compiled the Siku Quanshu. Rejected British envoy Macartney's trade demands.
qianlong.lesson: Confidence at the peak made global change hard to see.

lin_zexu.name: Lin Zexu
lin_zexu.detail: Cracked down hard on opium, triggering the Opium War. Later demoted, but gathered information about the world.
lin_zexu.lesson: An official who tried to know the world.

hongxiuquan.name: Hong Xiuquan
hongxiuquan.detail: After failing the civil service exams, influenced by Christianity, he proclaimed himself a son of God and began a rebellion.
hongxiuquan.lesson: A frustrated scholar became the center of a vast rebellion.

cixi.name: Empress Dowager Cixi
cixi.role: De facto supreme ruler of Qing
cixi.detail: Held real power for nearly half a century as regent for the Tongzhi and Guangxu emperors. Suppressed the Hundred Days' Reform but turned to reform late in life.
cixi.lesson: A ruler torn between conservatism and reform.

lihongzhang.name: Li Hongzhang
lihongzhang.detail: Promoted the Self-Strengthening Movement and built the Beiyang Fleet, but lost the Sino-Japanese War and signed the Treaty of Shimonoseki.
lihongzhang.lesson: Modernization efforts did not come in time.

lakshmibai.name: Lakshmibai
lakshmibai.detail: In the Indian Rebellion, personally led troops against the British and died in battle.
lakshmibai.lesson: Still remembered as a symbol of resistance.

tagore.name: Tagore
tagore.detail: Won the Nobel Prize in Literature, the first Asian to do so, for Gitanjali. Wrote the national anthems of both India and Bangladesh.
tagore.lesson: He built a bridge of words from East to the world.

liang_qichao.name: Liang Qichao
liang_qichao.detail: Took part in the Hundred Days' Reform, fled to Japan, enlightened through newspapers, and spread the idea of the nation-state in China.
liang_qichao.lesson: He nurtured national consciousness through the press.

luxun.name: Lu Xun
luxun.detail: In The True Story of Ah Q and Diary of a Madman, sharply depicted the ills of Chinese society. Studied in Sendai.
luxun.lesson: He tried to change the nation's spirit through literature.

chiang.name: Chiang Kai-shek
chiang.role: Leader of the Republic of China
chiang.detail: Unified China through the Northern Expedition and led the Second Sino-Japanese War. Lost the civil war and moved to Taiwan.
chiang.lesson: He led the nation between unification and civil war.

zhouenlai.name: Zhou Enlai
zhouenlai.role: Premier of the People's Republic of China
zhouenlai.detail: Supported Mao and handled diplomacy and practical affairs. Also played a major role at the Bandung Conference and in improving US-China relations.
zhouenlai.lesson: A coordinator beside a forceful leader.

yi_sunsin.name: Yi Sun-sin
yi_sunsin.detail: In the Imjin War, repeatedly defeated the Japanese navy using turtle ships and other means. Killed at the Battle of Noryang.
yi_sunsin.lesson: Tactics and preparation overturned inferior odds.

sejong.name: Sejong
sejong.detail: Led the creation of Hangul and promoted science, technology and music.
sejong.lesson: A king who made a script for the people.
